title.zh: 卷61 薛安都 畢衆敬 沈文秀 張讜 田益宗 孟表
title.en: Volume 61: Xue Andou, Bi Zhongjing, Shen Wenxiu, Zhang Dang, Tian Yizong, Meng Biao
title.raw: 卷61 薛安都 畢衆敬 沈文秀 張讜 田益宗 孟表 Volume 61: Xue Andou, Bi Zhongjing, Shen Wenxiu, Zhang Dang, Tian Yizong, Meng Biao

sentences.zh: 薛安都 畢眾敬 沈文秀 張讜 田益宗 孟表

translations.literal: Xue Andou; Bi Zhongjing; Shen Wenxiu; Zhang Dang; Tian Yizong; Meng Biao
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou; Bi Zhongjing; Shen Wenxiu; Zhang Dang; Tian Yizong; Meng Biao

sentences.zh: 薛安都，字休達，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Andou, courtesy name Xiuda, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou, whose courtesy name was Xiuda, came from Fenyin in Hedong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父廣，司馬德宗上黨太守。

translations.literal: His father Guang was governor of Shangdang under Sima Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang had served Sima Dezong as governor of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 安都少驍勇，善騎射，頗結輕俠，諸兄患之。

translations.literal: Andou in youth was fierce and brave, skilled at mounted archery, and inclined to consort with swaggering swordsmen; his elder brothers were troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Andou was bold and skilled in horsemanship and archery; he cultivated ties with roaming bravos, to his brothers' dismay.

sentences.zh: 安都乃求以一身分出，不取片資，兄許之，居於別廐。

translations.literal: Andou then asked to split off with only his own person, taking not a shred of the family property; his brothers agreed, and he lived in a separate stable-yard.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave the household with nothing but himself, claiming no share of the estate; his brothers consented, and he moved to an outbuilding.

sentences.zh: 遠近交遊者爭有送遺，馬牛衣服什物充牣其庭。

translations.literal: Friends near and far vied to send him gifts, and horses, cattle, clothing, and sundries filled his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Companions from near and far showered him with gifts until horses, cattle, clothes, and gear packed his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 真君五年，與東雍州刺史沮渠秉謀逆，[1]事發，奔於劉義隆。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenjun, he plotted rebellion with Juqu Bing, governor of Eastern Yong Province;[1] when the affair was exposed, he fled to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun year five he conspired with Eastern Yong governor Juqu Bing;[1] when the plot was discovered, he fled to Liu Yilong's court.

sentences.zh: 後自盧氏入寇弘農，執太守李拔等，遂逼陝城。

translations.literal: Later he raided Hongnong from Lushi, seized Grand Administrator Li Ba and others, and pressed on toward Shan Prefecture city.
translations.idiomatic: He later invaded Hongnong from Lushi, captured Grand Administrator Li Ba and others, and drove toward Shan city.

sentences.zh: 時秦州刺史杜道生討安都。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Province Governor Du Daosheng attacked Andou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Province governor Du Daosheng was then campaigning against him.

sentences.zh: 仍執拔等南遁，及世祖臨江，拔乃得還。

translations.literal: He still held Ba and the others as he fled south; only when Emperor Shizu came to the river did Ba return home.
translations.idiomatic: Still holding Ba and the rest, he fled south; Li Ba was able to return only after Emperor Shizu reached the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 安都在南，以武力見敍，值劉駿起江州，遂以為將，位至左衞率。

translations.literal: Andou in the south was rewarded for martial prowess; when Liu Jun rose in Jiang Province, he was made a general and rose to Left Guard Leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the south his fighting won him rank; when Liu Jun raised forces in Jiang Province, Andou entered his service and rose to Left Guard Leader.

sentences.zh: 劉昶歸降，子業以安都為平北將軍、徐州刺史，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: When Liu Chang surrendered, Ziye made Andou General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Xu Province, stationed at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Chang's surrender, Emperor Qianfei (Ziye) appointed Andou General Who Pacifies the North and Xu governor, with his seat at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，劉彧殺其主子業而自立，羣情不協，共立子業弟晉安王子勛，安都與沈文秀、崔道固、常珍奇等舉兵應之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, Liu Yu killed his lord Ziye and seized the throne; popular sentiment was divided, and they jointly enthroned Ziye's younger brother, the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun; Andou with Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu, Chang Zhenqi, and others raised troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping year six Liu Yu murdered Emperor Qianfei and took power; the realm split, enthroning Ziye's brother Prince of Jin'an Zixun, and Andou joined Shen Wenxiu, Cui Daogu, Chang Zhenqi, and others in arms for him.

sentences.zh: 彧遣將張永討安都，安都遣使來降，請兵救援。

translations.literal: Yu sent the general Zhang Yong against Andou; Andou sent envoys to surrender and begged for rescue troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Zhang Yong against him; Andou dispatched envoys offering surrender and pleading for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 顯祖召羣臣議之，羣官咸曰：「昔世祖常有并義隆之心，故親御六軍，遠臨江浦。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu summoned the ministers to deliberate; the officials all said: "Formerly Emperor Shizu often intended to annex Yilong's realm, and so personally led the Six Armies far to the river's bank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu called the court to counsel; officials said in unison: "Emperor Shizu long meant to swallow Yilong's domain and once led the Six Armies in person to the Jiang shore.

sentences.zh: 今江南阻亂，內外離心，安都今者求降，千載一會，機事難遇，時不可逢，取亂侮亡，於是乎在。」

translations.literal: Now the south is obstructed by disorder, inner and outer hearts are sundered; Andou at this moment seeks surrender—a meeting once in a thousand years. Such opportunity is hard to meet, the time cannot be missed; to take advantage of disorder and strike the perishing lies herein."
translations.idiomatic: The south is in turmoil and the court divided; Andou's offer is a chance that comes once in ages. Opportunity is fleeting—we must seize disorder and humble the doomed."

sentences.zh: 顯祖納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 安都又遣第四子道次為質，并與李敷等書，絡繹相繼。

translations.literal: Andou also sent his fourth son Daoci as hostage, and letters to Li Fu and others came in an unbroken stream.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his fourth son Daoci as hostage and wrote Li Fu and others in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 乃遣鎮東大將軍、博陵公尉元，城陽公孔伯恭等率騎一萬赴之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Grand General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Boling Wei Yuan, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, and others leading ten thousand horsemen to hurry to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand General Who Pacifies the East Duke of Boling Wei Yuan, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, and others with ten thousand cavalry to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 拜安都使持節，散騎常侍，都督徐、南、北兗、青、冀五州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事，鎮南大將軍，徐州刺史，賜爵河東公。

translations.literal: Andou was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant in the Scattered Cavalry, Commander over military affairs in Xu, southern, northern, and both Yan Provinces, Qing, Ji, and Liang Commandery in Yu, General Who Guards the South, governor of Xu, and enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Andou received the staff of authority, became Palace Attendant among the Scattered Cavalry, took command of Xu and five other provinces plus Liang in Yu, was named General Who Guards the South and Xu governor, and was created Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 安都以事窘歸國，元等既入彭城，安都乃中悔，謀圖元等，欲還以城叛，會元知之，遂不果發。

translations.literal: Andou, pressed by events, had returned to the realm; after Yuan and the rest entered Pengcheng, Andou repented midway and plotted against Yuan, intending to turn the city in rebellion again; Yuan learned of it, and the plot never came off.
translations.idiomatic: Andou had come back in straits; once Yuan entered Pengcheng, Andou wavered and schemed against him, planning to hand the city back to the enemy, but Yuan discovered it and the coup failed.

sentences.zh: 安都因重貨元等，委罪於女壻裴祖隆，元乃殺祖隆而隱安都謀。

translations.literal: Andou therefore lavished bribes on Yuan and the rest, shifting blame onto his son-in-law Pei Zulong; Yuan killed Zulong and concealed Andou's design.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed Yuan heavily and pinned the plot on his son-in-law Pei Zulong; Yuan executed Zulong and kept Andou's treachery secret.

sentences.zh: 皇興二年，與畢眾敬朝于京師，大見禮重，子姪羣從並處上客，皆封侯，至于門生無不收敍焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangxing, he and Bi Zhongjing attended court in the capital and was greatly honored; sons, nephews, and clansmen were all treated as chief guests and enfeoffed as marquises—even his students received appointments without exception.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing year two he and Bi Zhongjing came to the capital and received exceptional honor; kin and clients alike were lodged as chief guests and made marquises, and even his pupils won posts.

sentences.zh: 又為起第宅，館宇崇麗，資給甚厚。

translations.literal: A mansion was also built for him, its halls lofty and splendid, with very generous provision.
translations.idiomatic: The court raised him a residence of grand halls and supplied him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、秦州刺史、河東王，[2]諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made General of the original rank, governor of Qin, Prince of Hedong,[2] posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made general of his former rank, Qin governor, and Prince of Hedong;[2] his posthumous name was Kang.

sentences.zh: 子道標，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Daobiao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daobiao succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 太和初，出為鎮南將軍、平州刺史，治有聲稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he went out as General Who Guards the South and governor of Ping Province, and his governance won praise.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he became General Who Guards the South and Ping governor, winning a reputation for good rule.

sentences.zh: 轉相州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Xiang Province, general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Xiang governor while keeping his generalship.

sentences.zh: 復以本將軍為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Again with his former general's title he became governor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Qin governor with the same general's rank.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子達，字宗胤，襲，例降為侯。

translations.literal: His son Da, courtesy name Zongyin, succeeded; by precedent the title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Da, courtesy name Zongyin, inherited; by rule the rank fell to marquis.

sentences.zh: 及開建五等，以安都著勳先朝，封達河東郡開國侯，食邑八百戶。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, because Andou's merit in the former reign was outstanding, Da was enfeoffed Marquis of Hedong Commandery with an estate of eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five-rank system opened, Andou's service under the prior emperor won Da the Hedong commandery marquisate at eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後以河東畿甸，改封華陰縣侯。

translations.literal: Later, because Hedong lay in the metropolitan circuit, he was re-enfeoffed Marquis of Huayin County.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Hedong was in the capital region, the fief was changed to Huayin county marquis.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，拜奉車都尉，[3]出為漢陽太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he was made Bearer of the Imperial Carriage;[3] he went out as governor of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiping he became Bearer of the Imperial Carriage[3] and then Hanyang governor.

sentences.zh: 達不樂為郡，詔聽解。

translations.literal: Da disliked serving as governor; an edict allowed him to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Da disliked provincial office; the throne released him from the post.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子承華，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chenghua inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chenghua succeeded.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司徒從事中郎、河東邑中正。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Masters of Writing in the Secretariat and chief rectifier of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretariat attendant and chief rectifier for Hedong.

sentences.zh: 卒於安南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died as General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died holding the posts of General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子羅漢，襲。

translations.literal: His son Luohan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luohan inherited.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, noble titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, ranks were lowered as usual.

sentences.zh: 道標弟道異，亦以勳為第一客。

translations.literal: Daobiao's younger brother Daoyi likewise, for his merit, was a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: Daobiao's brother Daoyi, also honored for merit, ranked as a chief guest.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died early.

sentences.zh: 贈寧西將軍、秦州刺史、安邑侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Qin, and Marquis of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the West, Qin governor, and Marquis of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 道異弟道次。

translations.literal: Daoyi's younger brother Daoci.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyi's younger brother was Daoci.

sentences.zh: 既質京師，拜南中郎將、給事中，賜爵安邑侯，加安遠將軍。

translations.literal: After he was sent as hostage to the capital, he was made General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Palace, Gentleman at the Palace Gate, enfeoffed Marquis of Anyi, and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital as hostage, he became General of the Southern Gentlemen of the Palace and Gentleman at the Palace Gate, was created Marquis of Anyi, and added General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 出為安西將軍、秦州刺史、假河南公。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West, governor of Qin, and Acting Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West, Qin governor, and Acting Duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年，為光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year fifteen he became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and died.

sentences.zh: 子巒，襲爵，降為平溫子。

translations.literal: His son Luan inherited the title, reduced to Viscount of Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan succeeded, the title lowered to Viscount of Pingwen.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎、秦州刺史、鎮遠將軍、隴西鎮將，帶隴西太守。

translations.literal: He was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, governor of Qin, General Who Pacifies the Distance, garrison commander of Longxi, and concurrent governor of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretariat gentleman, Qin governor, General Who Pacifies the Distance, Longxi garrison commander, and concurrent Longxi governor.

sentences.zh: 後為滎陽太守，遷平北將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was governor of Xingyang, then promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Si.
translations.idiomatic: Later he governed Xingyang, then became General Who Pacifies the North and Si governor.

sentences.zh: 所在貪穢，在州彌甚。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was greedy and corrupt, and in the province it was worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Every post he held was marked by graft, worst of all in the province.

sentences.zh: 納賄於司空劉騰，以求美官，未得而騰死。

translations.literal: He bribed the Minister of Works Liu Teng seeking a fine office, but before he gained it Teng died.
translations.idiomatic: He paid Liu Teng, Minister of Works, for a better appointment, but Teng died before it came through.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，莫折念生反於秦州，遣其別帥卜胡、王慶雲等眾寇涇州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguang, Moqi Niansheng rebelled in Qin and sent his lieutenants Buhu, Wang Qingyun, and others with a host to raid Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguang year five Moqi Niansheng rose in Qin and sent lieutenants Buhu and Wang Qingyun against Jing.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以巒為持節、光祿大夫、假安南將軍、西道別將，與伊瓫生等討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong made Luan Bearer of the Staff, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting General Who Pacifies the South, and Separate Commander of the Western Route, to campaign with Yi Qiusheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong gave Luan the staff, made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Acting General Who Pacifies the South as Separate Commander of the Western Route, and sent him with Yi Qiusheng against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 進及平涼郡東，與賊交戰，不利，巒等退還。

translations.literal: Advancing to the east of Pingliang Commandery, he engaged the bandits and fared ill; Luan and the rest withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He met the rebels east of Pingliang, was defeated, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 後為撫軍將軍、汧城大都督，鎮北隴。

translations.literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Commander of Qian city, garrisoning the northern Long.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Commander of Qian city, guarding north Long.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年春，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Xiaochang he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xiaochang year two he died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 贈征西大將軍、雍州刺史，子如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Conquers the West and governor of Yong; his son's title was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Conquers the West and Yong governor; his son kept the title.

sentences.zh: 安都兄子碩明，隨安都入國，賜爵蒲坂侯，清河太守、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Andou's elder brother's son Shuoming followed Andou into the realm and was enfeoffed Marquis of Puban, governor of Qinghe and Grand Master for the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's nephew Shuoming followed him to Wei and was made Marquis of Puban, Qinghe governor, and Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 安都從祖弟真度。

translations.literal: Andou's younger clansman cousin Zhendu.
translations.idiomatic: Andou's cousin Zhendu.

sentences.zh: 初與安都南奔，及安都為徐州，真度為長史，頗有勇幹，為其爪牙。

translations.literal: At first he fled south with Andou; when Andou held Xu Province, Zhendu was chief clerk, quite brave and capable, and served as his strong arm.
translations.idiomatic: He had fled south with Andou; when Andou governed Xu, Zhendu was chief clerk, bold and able, his right hand.

sentences.zh: 從安都來降，為上客。

translations.literal: He followed Andou in surrender and was treated as a chief guest.
translations.idiomatic: He came over with Andou and was honored as a chief guest.

sentences.zh: 太和初，賜爵河北侯，加安遠將軍，為鎮遠將軍、平州刺史，假陽平公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was enfeoffed Marquis of Hebei, given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance, made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Ping governor, and Acting Duke of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe he was created Marquis of Hebei and General Who Pacifies the Distance, made Ping governor, and Acting Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 後降侯為伯，除冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later his marquisate was reduced to a barony and he was made General Who Champions the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later the marquisate became a barony and he was named General Who Champions the Army.

sentences.zh: 隨駕南討，假平南將軍。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial campaign south and was given the acting title General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he held the acting rank General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 久之，除護南蠻校尉、平南將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: After a time he was made Colonel Protector of the Southern Man, General Who Pacifies the South, and governor of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became Colonel Protector of the Southern Man, General Who Pacifies the South, and Jing governor.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾雍州刺史曹虎之詐降也，詔真度督四將出襄陽，無功而還。

translations.literal: When Xiao Ze's Yong Province governor Cao Huzhi feigned surrender, an edict ordered Zhendu to lead four generals out from Xiangyang; they returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Huzhi of Yong feigned surrender to Xiao Ze, Zhendu was ordered to lead four generals from Xiangyang and came back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 後征赭陽，為房伯玉所敗。

translations.literal: Later in the assault on Zheyang he was defeated by Fang Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, attacking Zheyang, he was beaten by Fang Boyu.

sentences.zh: 有司奏免官爵。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to strip his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities recommended removing his rank and posts.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔曰：「真度之罪，誠如所奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu's edict said: "Zhendu's offenses are indeed as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu replied: "Zhendu's faults are as reported.

sentences.zh: 但頃與安都送款彭方，開闢徐宋，外捍沈攸、道成之師，內寧邊境烏合之眾，淮海來服，功頗在茲。

translations.literal: Yet not long ago, with Andou he offered allegiance at Peng, opened Xu and Song, held off the armies of Shen You and Xiao Daocheng abroad, and within pacified the motley border bands; the Huai-Hai submitted—his merit lies chiefly here.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately, with Andou, he surrendered at Peng, secured Xu and Song, blocked Shen You and Xiao Daocheng abroad, and quieted the border within; the Huai and Hai came over—credit belongs there.

sentences.zh: 言念厥績，每用嘉美，赭陽百敗，何足計也。

translations.literal: Recalling that service, I have often praised it; a hundred defeats at Zheyang are not worth counting.
translations.idiomatic: I remember that service with favor; a hundred losses at Zheyang weigh little.

sentences.zh: 宜異羣將，更申後效。

translations.literal: He should be distinguished from the other generals and given another chance to prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: Treat him apart from the rest and let him earn merit again.

sentences.zh: 可還其元勳之爵，復除荊州刺史，自餘徽號削奪，進足彰忠，退可明失。」

translations.literal: Return his founding rank, restore him as Jing governor, and strip away the remaining honorific titles; advancing him will be enough to display loyalty, and withdrawing them can make his fault clear."
translations.idiomatic: Return his founding rank, restore him as Jing governor, and strip away the remaining honorific titles; advancing him will be enough to display loyalty, and withdrawing them can make his fault clear."

sentences.zh: 尋除假節、假冠軍將軍、東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Acting Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Champions the Army, and governor of Eastern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Acting Bearer of the Staff, Acting General Who Champions the Army, and Eastern Jing governor.

sentences.zh: 初，遷洛後，真度每獻計於高祖，勸先取樊鄧，後攻南陽，故為高祖所賞，賜帛一百匹，又加持節，正號冠軍，改封臨晉縣開國公，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the move to Luoyang, Zhendu often offered plans to Emperor Gaozu, urging first to take Fan and Deng, then attack Nanyang; therefore the emperor rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk, again gave him the staff, made his title General Who Champions the Army in full, and changed his fief to Duke of Linjin county with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital shifted to Luoyang he often advised Gaozu to seize Fan and Deng before Nanyang; the emperor rewarded him with silk, restored the staff, confirmed him General Who Champions the Army, and made him Duke of Linjin at three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「獻忠盡心，人臣令節；

translations.literal: The edict said: "To offer loyalty with all one's heart is a minister's proper measure;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Wholehearted loyalty is a subject's duty;

sentences.zh: 標善賞功，有國徽範。

translations.literal: to mark and reward merit is a state's shining norm.
translations.idiomatic: to mark and reward merit is a state's bright standard.

sentences.zh: 故一言可以興邦，片辭可以喪國，得無遠錄前謀，以褒厥善。

translations.literal: Thus one word can raise a state, one phrase can ruin it—should we not far record his earlier counsel to praise his good?
translations.idiomatic: One word can raise a realm and one phrase destroy it—shall we not honor his earlier counsel?

sentences.zh: 真度爰自遷京，每在戎役，沔北之計，恒所與聞，知無不言，頗見採納。

translations.literal: Since the move to the capital Zhendu has been in every campaign; plans north of the Mian he has always shared—nothing he knew went unsaid, and much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the relocation he has served in every war; plans north of the Mian he always shared, and much was heeded.

sentences.zh: 及六師南邁，朕欲超據新野，羣情皆異，真度獨與朕同。

translations.literal: When the Six Armies marched south I wished to seize Xinye ahead of the rest; all opinion differed, but Zhendu alone agreed with me.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Armies went south I meant to take Xinye first; the court disagreed, but Zhendu alone sided with me.

sentences.zh: 撫蠻寧夷，實有勤績，可增邑二百戶。」

translations.literal: He has real merit in pacifying the Man and calming the Yi; add two hundred households to his fief."
translations.idiomatic: He has real merit in pacifying the Man and calming the Yi; add two hundred households to his fief."

sentences.zh: 轉征虜將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and governor of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Yu governor.

sentences.zh: 景明初，豫州大飢，真度表曰：「去歲不收，飢饉十五，今又災雪三尺，民人萎餧，無以濟之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming Yu suffered great famine; Zhendu memorialized: "Last year brought no harvest; famine afflicts half the people; now disaster snow lies three feet deep, the people are withered and starving, and there is no way to save them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingming famine struck Yu; Zhendu wrote: "Last year's failure left half the province starving; now snow three feet deep has left the people wasted—there is no relief.

sentences.zh: 臣輒日別出州倉米五十斛為粥，救其甚者。」

translations.literal: Your servant has daily set aside fifty hu of grain from the provincial granary for porridge to aid the worst cases."
translations.idiomatic: I have daily taken fifty hu from the provincial granary for gruel for the worst cases."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「真度所表，甚有憂濟百姓之意，宜在拯卹。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Zhendu's memorial shows deep concern to succor the people; relief should be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "His care for the people deserves relief.

sentences.zh: 陳郡儲粟雖復不多，亦可分贍。

translations.literal: Though Chen Commandery's stored grain is not abundant, it may still be divided.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's stores, though modest, may be shared.

sentences.zh: 尚書量賑以聞。」

translations.literal: Let the Masters of Writing measure relief and report."
translations.idiomatic: Have the Masters of Writing allocate aid and report back."

sentences.zh: 及裴叔業以壽春內附，詔真度率眾赴之。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye brought Shouchun over to the realm, an edict ordered Zhendu to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun, Zhendu was ordered thither with troops.

sentences.zh: 尋遷華州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to governor of Hua, general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Hua governor, keeping his generalship.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉荊州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he became governor of Jing, still with his former general's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he became Jing governor at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 入為大司農卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除平南將軍、揚州刺史，又以年老，聽子懷吉以本官隨行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was made General Who Pacifies the South and Yang governor; because of age, his son Huaiji was allowed to accompany him in the same office.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengshi's opening he became General Who Pacifies the South and Yang governor; being old, he was permitted his son Huaiji to serve beside him in the same rank.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍豫州刺史王超宗率眾圍逼小峴，真度遣兼統軍李叔仁等率步騎擊之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Yu governor Wang Chaozong led a host to press Xiaoxian; Zhendu sent the joint commander Li Shuren and others with infantry and cavalry to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chaozong of Yu, serving Xiao Yan, besieged Xiaoxian; Zhendu sent Li Shuren with foot and horse to attack.

sentences.zh: 超宗逆來拒戰，叔仁擊破之，俘斬三千。

translations.literal: Chaozong came out to meet them in battle; Shuren routed him, capturing and killing three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong met them in the field; Shuren broke him, taking three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，又改封敷西縣。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, given the additional title Palace Attendant in the Scattered Cavalry, and his fief changed to Fuxi county.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the added title Scattered-Cavalry Palace Attendant, and his fief became Fuxi county.

sentences.zh: 永平中卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In Yongping he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongping at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 賻帛四百匹、朝服一襲，贈左光祿大夫，常侍如故，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Burial gifts were four hundred bolts of silk and one suit of court dress; posthumously he was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attendant title unchanged, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave four hundred bolts of silk and a court robe; posthumously he was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the same attendant rank, posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 有子十二人。

translations.literal: He had twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons.

sentences.zh: 嫡子懷徹，襲封。

translations.literal: The legitimate son Huaiche succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Huaiche inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 自太常丞，稍遷征虜將軍、中散大夫，又除左將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: From aide in the Grand Temple he was gradually promoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Palace Scattered Cavalier Grandee, then made Left General and Palace Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Grand Temple aide to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Scattered-Cavalry Grandee, then Left General and Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 卒於車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died as General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died holding the posts of General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 初，真度有女妓數十人，每集賓客，輒命奏之，絲竹歌舞，不輟於前，盡聲色之適。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhendu had several dozen female entertainers; whenever he gathered guests he would order them to perform—strings, bamboo, song, and dance unceasing before him, indulging every pleasure of sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu kept dozens of singing girls; at every gathering he had music and dance before him, savoring every delight.

sentences.zh: 庶長子懷吉居喪過周，以父妓十餘人并樂器獻之，世宗納焉。

translations.literal: The eldest son by a concubine, Huaiji, exceeded the mourning period; he presented more than ten of his father's entertainers together with instruments, and Emperor Shizong accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiji, a concubine's eldest son, overstay mourning and gave the emperor a dozen of his father's girls and their instruments.

sentences.zh: 懷吉，好勇有膂力，雖不善書學，亦解達世事。

translations.literal: Huaiji loved valor and had great strength; though not skilled in letters, he understood worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiji was bold and powerful; though no scholar, he grasped affairs.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請，歷直後寢，領太官令。

translations.literal: From Court Gentleman he passed through duty in the Rear Quarters and headed the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Court Gentleman, served in the rear palace, and became Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 正始初，為驃騎將軍，後試守恒農郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was made General of the Agile Cavalry; later he was tried as acting governor of Hengnong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengshi he became General of the Agile Cavalry, later acting Hengnong governor.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣眾入寇徐兗，安東邢巒討之，詔懷吉以本任為巒軍司。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent a host to raid Xu and Yan; Xing Luan of Andong campaigned against them, and an edict made Huaiji army secretary to Luan in his present rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan invaded Xu and Yan, Xing Luan was sent against him and Huaiji became his army secretary.

sentences.zh: 永平初，分梁州晉壽為益州，除征虜將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping, Jinshou in Liang was split off as Yi Province; he was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Yi governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping Jinshou became Yi Province and he was named its governor and General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 以元愉未平，中山王英為征東將軍討之，詔懷吉為英軍司，未發而愉平。

translations.literal: Because Yuan Yu was not yet pacified, Prince of Zhongshan Ying was made General Who Conquers the East to subdue him; Huaiji was ordered as Ying's army secretary, but before they marched Yu submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu's rebellion sent Prince Ying east with Huaiji as secretary; Yu surrendered before they set out.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將寇陷郢州之三關，詔英南討，懷吉仍為軍司。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's generals seized the three passes of Ying; Ying was ordered south and Huaiji again served as army secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan took Ying's three passes, Ying marched south and Huaiji went as his secretary again.

sentences.zh: 以義陽危急，令懷吉馳驛先赴。

translations.literal: Because Yiyang was critical, Huaiji was ordered to gallop ahead by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: With Yiyang in peril, he was sent ahead at full speed.

sentences.zh: 時豫州城民白早生殺刺史，以懸瓠入蕭衍，衍將齊苟仁率眾守城，於是自懸瓠以南至于安陸，惟義陽一城而已。

translations.literal: At the time the people of Yu Province city killed the governor and handed Xuancheng to Xiao Yan; Yan's general Qi Gouren held the city with a host, so from Xuancheng south to Anlu only Yiyang remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yu city's people killed their governor for Xiao Yan; Qi Gouren held Xuancheng, and south of it only Yiyang still stood.

sentences.zh: 懷吉與郢州刺史婁悅督厲將士，且守且戰，卒全義陽，與英討復三關諸戍。

translations.literal: Huaiji with Ying governor Lou Yue urged the troops, defending and fighting together, and finally preserved Yiyang; with Ying he recovered the garrisons of the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiji and Lou Yue held Yiyang through attack and defense, then with Ying retook the three passes.

sentences.zh: 後鎮東將軍盧昶救朐山，與賊相持，詔懷吉為昶軍司。

translations.literal: Later General Who Pacifies the East Lu Chang relieved Qushan and locked with the enemy; Huaiji was ordered as Chang's army secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Chang relieved Qushan, Huaiji became his army secretary.

sentences.zh: 及昶敗，懷吉得不坐。

translations.literal: When Chang was defeated, Huaiji was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang's defeat he escaped blame.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，以本將軍除梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yan chang he was made governor of Liang with his former general's title.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan chang he became Liang governor at the same rank.

sentences.zh: 南秦氐反，攻逼武興，懷吉遣長史崔纂、司馬韋弼、別駕范珦擊平之。

translations.literal: The Di of Southern Qin rebelled and pressed Wuxing; Huaiji sent Chief Clerk Cui Zuan, Marshal Wei Bi, and Registrar Fan Xian to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Qin Di rebels threatened Wuxing; his staff Cui Zuan, Wei Bi, and Fan Xian crushed them.

sentences.zh: 進號右將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to Right General.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right General.

sentences.zh: 正光初，除後將軍、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang he was made Rear General and Fen governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguang he became Rear General and Fen governor.

sentences.zh: 四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was General Who Pacifies the North and Bing governor.

sentences.zh: 懷吉本不厲清節，及為汾州，偏有聚納之響。

translations.literal: Huaiji had never been strict in integrity; as Fen governor he especially gained a reputation for amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He was never austere; in Fen he was notorious for graft.

sentences.zh: 自以支庶，餌誘勝己，共為婚姻。

translations.literal: As a collateral branch he courted his betters and contracted marriages with them.
translations.idiomatic: A cadet line, he flattered the powerful and married into their houses.

sentences.zh: 多攜親戚，悉令同行，兼為之彌縫，恣其取受。

translations.literal: He brought many kinsmen, all made to travel with him, and smoothed matters for them, letting them take what they wished.
translations.idiomatic: He took kin along everywhere, covering their excesses.

sentences.zh: 而將勞賓客，曲盡物情，送去迎來，不避寒熱。

translations.literal: Yet he attended guests exhaustively, fulfilling every sentiment, seeing them off and welcoming them without regard to heat or cold.
translations.idiomatic: Still he entertained guests lavishly in every season.

sentences.zh: 性少言，每有接對，但默然而退。

translations.literal: By nature he spoke little; whenever he received someone he only withdrew in silence.
translations.idiomatic: He was taciturn and often met visitors only to retire without words.

sentences.zh: 既指授先期，人馬之數，左右密已記錄。

translations.literal: Once he had given prior instructions, the numbers of men and horses were secretly recorded by those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed numbers of men and horses beforehand; attendants noted them quietly.

sentences.zh: 俄而酒饌相尋，芻粟繼至，逮于將別，贈以錢縑，下及厮傭，咸過本望。

translations.literal: Soon wine and food followed in succession, fodder and grain arrived one after another, and when they were about to part he gave money and silk—even down to servants—all exceeding expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Feasts and fodder poured in; on leaving he gave cash and silk to everyone down to servants, beyond hope.

sentences.zh: 其延納貴賤若此。

translations.literal: Thus he entertained high and low alike.
translations.idiomatic: He treated nobles and commoners the same way.

sentences.zh: 懷吉弟懷直，京兆內史、衞大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Huaiji's younger brother Huaizhi was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, General of the Guard, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Huaizhi was Jingzhao metropolitan governor, Guard General, and Left Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 懷直弟懷朴，恒農太守、襄陵男。

translations.literal: Huaizhi's younger brother Huai Pu was governor of Hengnong and Baron of Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Younger still, Huai Pu was Hengnong governor and Baron of Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 懷朴弟懷景，征南將軍、河東太守、安定男。

translations.literal: Huai Pu's younger brother Huaijing was General Who Conquers the South, Hedong governor, and Baron of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijing was General Who Conquers the South, Hedong governor, and Baron of Anding.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈持節、都督北徐兗東徐三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over military affairs in northern Xu, Yan, and eastern Xu, General of the Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Xu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the staff, command of three eastern provinces, General of the Agile Cavalry, Three Excellencies honors, and Xu governorship.

sentences.zh: 懷景弟懷儁，撫軍將軍、光祿大夫、汾陰男。

translations.literal: Huaijing's younger brother Huaijun was General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Baron of Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijun was General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Baron of Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 出為征南將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Conquers the South and Yi governor.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as southern conqueror and Yi governor.

sentences.zh: 天平初，代還至梁州，與刺史元羅俱為蕭衍將蘭欽所擒，送江南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, returning from his replacement, he reached Liang with Governor Yuan Luo and was both seized by Xiao Yan's general Lan Qin and sent to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianping, he and Yuan Luo were captured in Liang by Lan Qin and sent to the south.

sentences.zh: 衍見懷儁，謂之曰：「卿父先為魏荊州，我于時猶在襄陽，且州壤連接，極相知練。

translations.literal: Yan saw Huaijun and said to him: "Your father once held Wei Jing; I was then still at Xiangyang, and our provinces adjoined—we knew each other well.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan told him: "Your father governed Jing for Wei while I was at Xiangyang—we knew each other well.

sentences.zh: 卿今至此，當能住乎？

translations.literal: Now that you have come here, can you stay?
translations.idiomatic: Can you stay now?

sentences.zh: 若欲還者，亦以禮相遣。」

translations.literal: If you wish to return, I will also send you off with courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to go home, I will release you honorably."

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「此家在北，富貴極不可言。」

translations.literal: He turned to his attendants and said: "This family in the north—their wealth is beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: He told his staff: "This house in the north is unimaginably rich."

sentences.zh: 懷儁便乞歸，衍聽還國。

translations.literal: Huaijun then begged to return, and Yan allowed him to go home.
translations.idiomatic: Huaijun asked to leave and Yan let him return.

sentences.zh: 興和中卒。

translations.literal: He died in Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 子湛儒，襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhanru succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhanru inherited.

sentences.zh: 武定中，司空水曹參軍。

translations.literal: In Wuding he was an aide in the Water Bureau of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding he served the Works ministry's Water Bureau.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, noble titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took power, ranks fell as usual.

sentences.zh: 真度諸子既多，其母非一，同產相朋，因有憎愛。

translations.literal: Zhendu's sons were many and their mothers not one; those of the same mother banded together, and there arose likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu had many sons by different mothers; full brothers cliqued and feuded.

sentences.zh: 興和中，遂致訴列，云以毒藥相害，顯在公府，發揚疵釁。

translations.literal: In Xinghe they brought suits charging one another with poison, openly in the government offices, airing every fault.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe they sued one another for poisoning before the whole court.

sentences.zh: 時人耻焉。

translations.literal: Men of the time were ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries were disgusted.

sentences.zh: 畢眾敬，小名捺，東平須昌人。

translations.literal: Bi Zhongjing, pet name Na, was a man of Xuchang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing, called Na, came from Xuchang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬射獵，交結輕果，常於疆境盜掠為業。

translations.literal: In youth he loved bow, horse, hunting, and shooting, consorted with daredevils, and often made border raiding his trade.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he hunted and rode with daredevils, raiding across the border for a living.

sentences.zh: 劉駿為徐兗刺史，辟為部從事。

translations.literal: When Liu Jun was governor of Xu and Yan, he recruited him as a section aide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun as Xu-Yan governor took him as a section aide.

sentences.zh: 駿既竊號，歷其泰山太守、冗從僕射。

translations.literal: After Jun seized the throne, he served successively as Taishan governor and Supernumerary Attendant in the Retinue.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun took the throne, Zhongjing became Taishan governor and a supernumerary attendant.

sentences.zh: 及劉彧殺子業而自立，遣眾敬出詣兗州募人。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu killed Ziye and took power, he sent Zhongjing out to Yan to raise men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent him to Yan to recruit after killing Ziye.

sentences.zh: 到彭城，刺史薛安都召與密謀，云：「晉安有上流之名，且孝武第三子，當共卿為計西從。」

translations.literal: At Pengcheng, Governor Xue Andou summoned him and plotted secretly with him, saying: "Jin’an has the reputation of being upstream, and he is also Emperor Xiaowu’s third son; together with you, we should plan to follow him west."
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng, Governor Xue Andou summoned him and plotted secretly with him, saying: "Jin’an has the reputation of being upstream, and he is also Emperor Xiaowu’s third son; together with you, we should plan to follow him west."

sentences.zh: 乃矯彧命，以眾敬行兗州事，眾敬從之。

translations.literal: He then forged Yu's order making Zhongjing act as Yan governor, and Zhongjing obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He forged Liu Yu's order naming Zhongjing acting Yan governor, and Zhongjing obeyed.

sentences.zh: 時兗州刺史殷孝祖留其妻子，率文武二千人赴彧，使司馬劉文石守城。

translations.literal: At the time Yan governor Yin Xiaozu left wife and children behind and led two thousand officials and soldiers to Yu, leaving Marshal Liu Wenshi to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xiaozu left family in Yan and marched two thousand men to Liu Yu, leaving Liu Wenshi in the city.

sentences.zh: 眾敬率眾取瑕丘，殺文石。

translations.literal: Zhongjing led troops to take Xiaqiu and killed Wenshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing seized Xiaqiu and killed Wenshi.

sentences.zh: 安都與孝祖先不相協，命眾敬誅孝祖諸子，眾敬不得已，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Andou and Xiaozu had long been at odds; he ordered Zhongjing to execute Xiaozu's sons; Zhongjing had no choice and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Andou ordered Xiaozu's sons killed; Zhongjing reluctantly obeyed.

sentences.zh: 州內悉附，唯東平太守申纂據無鹽城不與之同。

translations.literal: All within the province submitted; only Dongping governor Shen Zuan held Wuyan city and would not join.
translations.idiomatic: The province followed him except Shen Zuan at Wuyan.

sentences.zh: 及彧平子勛，授纂兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yu pacified Zixun, he made Zuan Yan governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun's fall, Liu Yu made Zuan Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 會安都引國授軍經其城下，[4]纂閉門城守，深恨眾敬。

translations.literal: When Andou brought in the realm's relief army past his walls,[4] Zuan shut the gates and defended, deeply resenting Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Andou's Wei army passed below,[4] Zuan shut Wuyan and hated Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 會有人發眾敬父墓，遂令其母骸首散落。

translations.literal: Someone opened Zhongjing's father's tomb, scattering his mother's bones and head.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders opened his father's tomb and scattered his mother's remains.

sentences.zh: 眾敬發哀行服，拷掠近墓細民，死者十餘人。

translations.literal: Zhongjing mourned and wore sackcloth, torturing commoners near the tomb until more than ten died.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned and tortured villagers near the tomb, killing a dozen.

sentences.zh: 又疑纂所為，弟眾愛為安都長史，亦遣人密至濟陰，掘纂父墓以相報答。

translations.literal: Suspecting Zuan, his younger brother Zhong'ai, Andou's chief clerk, also sent men secretly to Jiyin to dig up Zuan's father's tomb in reprisal.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed Zuan; brother Zhong'ai had Zuan's father's tomb dug at Jiyin in revenge.

sentences.zh: 及安都以城入國，眾敬不同其謀。

translations.literal: When Andou surrendered the city to the realm, Zhongjing did not agree to the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Andou meant to hand Pengcheng to Wei, Zhongjing refused.

sentences.zh: 子元賓以母并百口悉在彭城，恐交致禍，日夜啼泣，遣請眾敬，眾敬猶未從之。

translations.literal: His son Yuanbin, with mother and a hundred mouths all in Pengcheng, feared mutual ruin and wept day and night, sending pleas to Zhongjing, who still would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuanbin, whose kin were hostages in Pengcheng, begged him day and night; he still held back.

sentences.zh: 眾敬先已遣表謝彧，彧授眾敬兗州刺史，而以元賓有他罪，獨不捨之。

translations.literal: Zhongjing had already sent a memorial apologizing to Yu; Yu made him Yan governor but, because Yuanbin had another offense, alone would not pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: He had already apologized to Liu Yu, who made him governor but kept Yuanbin prisoner.

sentences.zh: 眾敬拔刀斫柱曰：「皓首之年，唯有此子，今不原貸，何用獨全！」

translations.literal: Zhongjing drew his sword and hacked a pillar, saying: "In my white-haired years this child is all I have—if he is not spared, why should I alone survive!"
translations.idiomatic: He struck a pillar with his sword: "In old age he is my only son—spare him or I am nothing!"

sentences.zh: 及尉元至，遂以城降。

translations.literal: When Wei Yuan arrived, he then surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yuan came, he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 元遣將入城，事定，眾敬悔恚，數日不食。

translations.literal: Yuan sent generals into the city; when it was settled, Zhongjing repented and raged, and for several days ate nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan entered, remorse kept him from food for days.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，就拜散騎常侍、寧南將軍、兗州刺史，賜爵東平公，與中書侍郎李璨對為刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing he was at once made Palace Attendant in the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the South, and Yan governor, enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping, paired with Secretariat Attendant Li Can as governors.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing's opening he became Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, Yan governor, and Duke of Dongping, paired with Li Can.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜攻克無鹽，申纂為亂兵所傷，走出被擒，送於白曜。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao took Wuyan; Shen Zuan was wounded by mutinous soldiers, fled out, and was captured and sent to Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao took Wuyan; Zuan was wounded, captured, and sent to Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 白曜無殺纂之意，而城中火起，纂創重不能避，為火所燒死。

translations.literal: Baiyao had no intent to kill Zuan, but fire broke out in the city; Zuan's wounds were grave and he could not escape and was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao meant no kill, but fire in the city trapped wounded Zuan and he burned.

sentences.zh: 眾敬聞克無鹽，懼不殺纂，乃與白曜書，并表朝廷，云「家之禍酷，皆由於纂」。

translations.literal: Hearing that Wuyan had been taken, Zhongjing feared that Zuan would not be killed, so he wrote to Baiyao and also memorialized the court, saying: "The cruelty of my family’s calamity was entirely caused by Zuan."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wuyan had been taken, Zhongjing feared that Zuan would not be killed, so he wrote to Baiyao and also memorialized the court, saying: "The cruelty of my family’s calamity was entirely caused by Zuan."

sentences.zh: 聞纂死，乃悅。

translations.literal: Hearing Zuan was dead, he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan died, he rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 二年，與薛安都朝于京師，因留之，賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: In the second year he and Xue Andou attended court in the capital and was detained, granted one fine mansion.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he came to court with Andou, was kept, and given a mansion.

sentences.zh: 後復為兗州刺史，將軍如故，徵還京師。

translations.literal: Later he was again Yan governor, general's title unchanged, then summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yan again, then was recalled.

sentences.zh: 眾敬善自奉養，食膳豐華，必致他方遠味。

translations.literal: Zhongjing knew how to care for himself; his meals were rich and splendid, and he always procured flavors from distant places.
translations.idiomatic: He lived well, dining on delicacies from afar.

sentences.zh: 年已七十，鬢髮皓白，而氣力未衰，跨鞍馳騁，有若少壯。

translations.literal: Though already seventy, his hair and beard were white, yet his strength had not declined; mounting the saddle and galloping, he was like a young man.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy his hair was white but he rode like a youth.

sentences.zh: 篤於姻類，深有國士之風，張讜之亡，躬往營視，有若至親。

translations.literal: He was devoted to kin and had the air of a true gentleman; when Zhang Dang died he went in person to arrange the funeral as if for close family.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in kinship and noble in manner, he buried Zhang Dang as kin.

sentences.zh: 太和中，高祖賓禮舊老，眾敬與咸陽公高允引至方山，雖文武奢儉，好尚不同，然亦與允甚相愛敬，接膝談款，有若平生。

translations.literal: In Taihe, Emperor Gaozu honored the old; Zhongjing with Duke of Xianyang Gao Yun were led to Mount Fang—though civil and military, luxury and thrift, and tastes differed, he also loved and respected Yun greatly, knee to knee in intimate talk as in earlier days.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fêted elders at Mount Fang; though unlike Gao Yun in taste, he loved him as of old.

sentences.zh: 後以篤老，乞還桑梓，朝廷許之。

translations.literal: Later, because of devoted old age, he begged to return home; the court permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to go home in old age and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 眾敬臨還，獻真珠璫四具、銀裝劍一口、刺虎矛一枚、仙人文綾一百匹。

translations.literal: On leaving, Zhongjing presented four pearl pendants, one silver-mounted sword, one tiger-slaying spear, and a hundred bolts of immortal-pattern brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving, he gave pearls, a silver sword, a spear, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 文明太后、高祖引見於皇信堂，賜以酒饌，車一乘、馬三匹、絹二百匹，勞遣之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wensheng and Emperor Gaozu received him in the Hall of Imperial Trust, bestowing wine and food, one carriage, three horses, and two hundred bolts of silk, and sent him off with honors.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and Gaozu feasted him, gave carriage, horses, and silk, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 十五年十月卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of year fifteen.

sentences.zh: 詔於兗州賜絹一千匹，以供葬事。

translations.literal: An edict granted a thousand bolts of silk in Yan Province for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave a thousand bolts of silk in Yan for his burial.

sentences.zh: 子元賓，少而豪俠，有武幹，涉獵書史。

translations.literal: His son Yuanbin in youth was bold and chivalrous, had martial talent, and ranged through books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuanbin was young, heroic, martial, and literate.

sentences.zh: 為劉駿正員將軍，與父同建勳誠。

translations.literal: He was a regular general under Liu Jun and with his father built loyal merit together.
translations.idiomatic: He had been Liu Jun's regular general and shared his father's service.

sentences.zh: 及至京師，俱為上客，賜爵須昌侯，加平遠將軍。

translations.literal: When they reached the capital both were chief guests; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xuchang and made General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital both were chief guests; he became Marquis of Xuchang and General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 後以元賓勳重，拜使持節、平南將軍、兗州刺史，假彭城公。

translations.literal: Later, because Yuanbin's merit was weighty, he was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Yan governor, and Acting Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the staff, southern command, Yan governorship, and Acting Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 父子相代為本州，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Father and son in succession held the home province—a glory of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son in turn governed Yan—the age's envy.

sentences.zh: 時眾敬以老還鄉，常呼元賓為使君。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongjing had returned home in old age and always called Yuanbin "my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing at home called Yuanbin "my lord."

sentences.zh: 每於元賓聽政之時，乘輿出至元賓所，先遣左右敕不聽起，觀其斷決，忻忻然喜見顏色。

translations.literal: Whenever Yuanbin held court, he would ride out to Yuanbin's place, first sending attendants to forbid his rising, watching his judgments, delighted in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to watch Yuanbin judge cases, forbidding him to rise, beaming with pride.

sentences.zh: 眾敬善持家業，尤能督課田產，大致儲積。

translations.literal: Zhongjing was good at managing the household and especially at supervising field work, amassing great stores.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the estate and fields and built vast stores.

sentences.zh: 元賓為政清平，善撫民物，百姓愛樂之。

translations.literal: Yuanbin's governance was clear and level, good at soothing the people, and the commoners loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbin ruled fairly and the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 以父憂解任，喪中遙授長兼殿中尚書。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he left office; during mourning he was remotely appointed acting Masters of Writing in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning but was named acting palace minister.

sentences.zh: 其年冬末卒。

translations.literal: At the end of that winter he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died late that winter.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、衞尉卿，諡曰平。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Minister of the Guard, posthumous name Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously General Who Pacifies the Army and Minister of the Guard, posthumous name Ping.

sentences.zh: 賜帛八百匹。

translations.literal: He was granted eight hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave eight hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 元賓入國，初娶東平劉氏，有四子，祖朽、祖髦、祖歸、祖旋；

translations.literal: When Yuanbin entered the realm he first married the Liu clan of Dongping and had four sons: Zuxiu, Zumao, Zugui, and Zuxuan;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbin first married a Liu of Dongping and had Zuxiu, Zumao, Zugui, and Zuxuan;

sentences.zh: 賜妻元氏生二子，祖榮、祖暉。

translations.literal: his granted wife of the Yuan clan bore two sons, Zurong and Zuhui.
translations.idiomatic: his imperial grant wife Yuan bore Zurong and Zuhui.

sentences.zh: 祖朽最長，祖暉次祖髦。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was eldest; Zuhui was junior to Zumao.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiu was oldest; Zuhui ranked below Zumao.

sentences.zh: 故事，前妻雖先有子，後賜之妻子皆承嫡。

translations.literal: By precedent, though the first wife had sons earlier, the sons of the later granted wife all inherited as legitimate.
translations.idiomatic: By rule, sons of the grant wife took precedence as heirs even if the first wife's sons were older.

sentences.zh: 所以劉氏先亡，祖暉不服重；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Liu clan died first, Zuhui did not wear full mourning;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu died first, Zuhui did not observe full mourning;

sentences.zh: 元氏後卒，祖朽等三年終禮。

translations.literal: when the Yuan clan died later, Zuxiu and the others completed the three-year rites.
translations.idiomatic: when Yuan died later, Zuxiu and the rest finished three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 祖榮早卒。

translations.literal: Zurong died young.
translations.idiomatic: Zurong died early.

sentences.zh: 子義允，襲祖爵東平公，例降為侯。

translations.literal: His son Yiyun inherited the grandfather's title Duke of Dongping, reduced by precedent to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yiyun inherited the Dongping dukedom, lowered to marquis.

sentences.zh: 陵江將軍、給事中，卒。

translations.literal: General Who Crosses the River, Gentleman at the Palace Gate—then he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was General Who Crosses the River and Palace Gate Gentleman, then died.

sentences.zh: 子僧安襲。

translations.literal: His son Seng'an succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Seng'an inherited.

sentences.zh: 祖朽，身長八尺，腰帶十圍，歷涉經史，好為文詠。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was eight feet tall with a ten-hand girdle, versed in classics and histories, fond of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiu stood eight feet, ten-hand waist, read classics, and wrote verse.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚，善與人交。

translations.literal: By nature generous and thick, skilled at friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed and made friends easily.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵須昌侯，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's Marquis of Xuchang, reduced by precedent to baron.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded as Marquis of Xuchang, then baron by rule.

sentences.zh: 起家員外郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as an outer aide.
translations.idiomatic: He started as an outer secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎、治書侍御史，加寧遠將軍，本州中正。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, investigating censor, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance and chief rectifier of the home province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as secretariat gentleman and censor, added General Who Pacifies the Distance and provincial rectifier.

sentences.zh: 正始三年，蕭衍將蕭及先率步騎二萬入寇兗州，及先令別帥角念屯于蒙山。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi, Xiao Yan's general Xiao Jixian led twenty thousand foot and horse to raid Yan; Jixian sent the lieutenant Jiaonian to camp at Mount Meng.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi year three Xiao Jixian invaded Yan with twenty thousand men and posted Jiaonian on Mount Meng.

sentences.zh: 以祖朽為統軍，假寧朔將軍，隸邢巒討之。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was made joint commander and Acting General Who Pacifies the North, subordinate to Xing Luan in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiu was joint commander under Xing Luan as Acting General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 祖朽開誘有方，降者相繼。

translations.literal: Zuxiu's inducements were well judged and surrenders came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: His offers brought steady surrenders.

sentences.zh: 賊出逆戰，祖朽大破之。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to fight and Zuxiu routed them.
translations.idiomatic: He met the rebels in the field and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 賊走還柵，祖朽夜又焚擊，賊徒潰散。

translations.literal: The bandits fled back to their palisade; Zuxiu at night burned and struck again and the rebels scattered.
translations.idiomatic: They fled to camp; he burned it by night and they broke.

sentences.zh: 追討百餘里，斬獲及赴沂水死者四千餘人，斬龍驤將軍矯道儀、寧朔將軍王季秀。

translations.literal: Pursuing over a hundred li, those slain, captured, and drowned in the Yi exceeded four thousand; he beheaded the Dragon Agile General Jiao Daoyi and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Jixiu.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred-li pursuit left four thousand dead or drowned in the Yi; he killed Jiao Daoyi and Wang Jixiu.

sentences.zh: 以功封南城縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Nancheng county with two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became Baron of Nancheng at two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 歷散騎侍郎、中書侍郎，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He passed through Scattered Cavalry Attendant and Secretariat Attendant, with the additional title Dragon Agile General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Scattered-Cavalry and Secretariat attendant and Dragon Agile General.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，安南王志出討荊沔，以祖朽為志軍司，兼給事黃門侍郎，尋遷司空長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Yan chang, General Who Pacifies the South Zhi campaigned against Jing and Mian; Zuxiu was Zhi's army secretary and concurrent Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Attending Affairs, then moved to chief clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yan chang he was army secretary to Zhi against Jing-Mian, then Works chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 神龜末，除持節、東豫州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the end of Shen gui he was made Bearer of the Staff and Eastern Yu governor, general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: At Shen gui's end he became Bearer of the Staff and Eastern Yu governor.

sentences.zh: 祖朽善撫邊人，清平有信，務在安靜，百姓稱之。

translations.literal: Zuxiu was good at soothing border people, clear and trustworthy, intent on quiet, and the commoners praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled the border fairly and quietly and won praise.

sentences.zh: 還，除前將軍、太尉長史、兼尚書北道行臺。

translations.literal: Returning, he was made Forward General, chief clerk of the Grand Minister, and concurrent Northern Route Commissioner of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was Forward General, Grand Minister chief clerk, and northern commissioner.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除持節、本將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang he was made Bearer of the Staff, general of his former rank, and southern Yan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang he took the staff as southern Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 尋授度支尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 行定州，未之職，改授安東將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Acting Ding governor—before taking post he was changed to General Who Pacifies the East and Ying governor.
translations.idiomatic: Named acting Ding governor, he became Ying governor before arriving.

sentences.zh: 為賊帥鮮于脩禮攻圍積旬，拒守自固。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli besieged him for weeks; he defended and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Xiuli besieged him weeks; he held out.

sentences.zh: 病卒於州。

translations.literal: He died of illness in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died ill in office.

sentences.zh: 贈衞將軍、吏部尚書、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General of the Guard, Minister of Personnel, and Yan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Guard General, Personnel Minister, and Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 祖朽無子，以弟祖歸子義暢為後，襲爵。

translations.literal: Zuxiu had no sons; his younger brother Zugui's son Yichang was made heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted brother Zugui's son Yichang.

sentences.zh: 義暢，傾巧無士業，善通時要。

translations.literal: Yichang was clever but without scholarly vocation, skilled at grasping the moment's needs.
translations.idiomatic: Yichang was shrewd, not scholarly, but politically adept.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎中、侍郎、兗州刺史、大中正、中軍將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He passed through Secretariat aide, vice minister, Yan governor, chief rectifier, General of the Central Army, and Direct Attendant in the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served secretariat, Yan, rectifier, Central Army general, and Direct Scattered-Cavalry Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，車騎將軍，尋除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was General of the Chariots and Cavalry, then made Scattered-Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang he was Chariots-and-Cavalry General, then Scattered-Cavalry Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天平中，坐與北豫州山賊張儉通，伏法。

translations.literal: In Tianping, for communicating with the mountain bandit Zhang Jian of northern Yu, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he was executed for collusion with Zhang Jian.

sentences.zh: 祖髦，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: Zumao began as Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Zumao began as Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 兄祖朽別封南城，以須昌侯回授之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zuxiu was separately enfeoffed at Nancheng and the Marquis of Xuchang was transferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuxiu took Nancheng, the Xuchang marquisate passed to Zumao.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，累遷揚烈將軍、東平太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shen gui he rose to General Who Raises the Fierce and Dongping governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shen gui he became General Who Raises the Fierce and Dongping governor.

sentences.zh: 後為本州別駕，卒於官。

translations.literal: Later he was the province's vice governor and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as provincial vice governor.

sentences.zh: 子義和，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yihe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yihe inherited.

sentences.zh: 卒於右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He died as Right General and Palace Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He died Right General and Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Yan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, eastern conqueror, and Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 子仁超。

translations.literal: His son Renchao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Renchao.

sentences.zh: 義和第六弟義亮，性豪疏。

translations.literal: Yihe's sixth younger brother Yiliang was bold and careless by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yihe's sixth brother Yiliang was reckless.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書郎、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He passed through Secretariat Gentleman and Secretariat Retainer.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretariat gentleman and retainer.

sentences.zh: 天平中，[5]與舍人韋鴻坐泄密，賜盡於宅。

translations.literal: In Tianping,[5] with Retainer Wei Hong he was convicted of leaking secrets and ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping[5] he and Wei Hong were executed at home for leaking secrets.

sentences.zh: 祖暉，早有器幹。

translations.literal: Zuhui early showed talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Zuhui showed talent early.

sentences.zh: 自奉朝請，稍遷鎮遠將軍、前軍將軍、直後。

translations.literal: From Court Gentleman he was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distance, Forward General, and duty in the Rear Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Court Gentleman to border general and rear-palace duty.

sentences.zh: 正始中，除龍驤將軍、東郡太守。

translations.literal: In Zhengshi he was made Dragon Agile General and Dongjun governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi he became Dragon Agile General and Dongjun governor.

sentences.zh: 入為驍騎將軍，加征虜將軍，後試守勃海郡。

translations.literal: He entered as Valiant Cavalry General with the added title General Who Conquers the Barbarians, later tried as acting Bohai governor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Valiant Cavalry General, added barbarian-conqueror, then acting Bohai governor.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，拜潁川太守。

translations.literal: In Xiping he was made Yingchuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping he governed Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，除右將軍、豳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shen gui he was made Right General and Bin governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shen gui he was Right General and Bin governor.

sentences.zh: 入為平東將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He entered as General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as eastern conqueror and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，豳州民反，招引隴賊，攻逼州城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguang the people of Bin rebelled, drawing Long bandits, and pressed the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguang year five Bin rose, Long rebels joined, and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 以祖暉前在州日得民情和，復授平西將軍、豳州刺史，假安西將軍，為別將以討之。

translations.literal: Because Zuhui in his former days in the province had won the people's harmony, he was again made General Who Pacifies the West and Bin governor, Acting General Who Pacifies the West, and Separate Commander to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled for his former popularity, he was sent back as Bin governor and western conqueror to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 祖暉且戰且前，突圍入治。

translations.literal: Zuhui fought while advancing and broke through into the seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: He fought his way into the city.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，北海王顥救至，城圍始解。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang Prince of Beihai Hao's relief arrived and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hao of Beihai relieved the city in Xiaochang's opening.

sentences.zh: 以全城之勳，封新昌縣開國子，食邑四百戶。

translations.literal: For the merit of preserving the whole city he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xinchang county with four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Saving the city won him Viscount of Xinchang at four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後值蕭寶夤退敗，祖暉乃拔城東趣華州，坐免官爵。

translations.literal: Later when Xiao Baoyin retreated in defeat, Zuhui abandoned the city and went east toward Hua, and sat stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin's defeat he abandoned Bin for Hua and lost rank.

sentences.zh: 尋假征虜將軍，行豳州事。

translations.literal: Soon he was Acting General Who Conquers the Barbarians, acting Bin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was acting barbarian-conqueror administering Bin.

sentences.zh: 建義中，詔復州爵，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: In Jianyi an edict restored his provincial title and added General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyi restored his rank and added General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 永安中，祖暉從大嶺柵規入州城。

translations.literal: In Yong'an Zuhui from the Great Ridge palisade planned to enter the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an he tried to re-enter Bin from Great Ridge.

sentences.zh: 于時賊帥叱干騏驎保太子壁，祖暉擊破之。

translations.literal: At the time the bandit chief Chigan Qilin held Taizi wall; Zuhui defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebel Chigan Qilin at Taizi wall.

sentences.zh: 而賊宿勤明達復攻祖暉，祖暉兵少糧竭，軍援不至，為賊所乘，遂歿，時年五十。

translations.literal: But the bandit Suqin Mingda again attacked Zuhui; Zuhui had few troops and grain was exhausted, relief did not come, the bandits seized their chance, and he perished, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Suqin Mingda returned; outnumbered and starving, without relief, he fell at fifty.

sentences.zh: 長子義勰，襲爵。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yixie inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Yixie succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武定中，開府中郎。

translations.literal: In Wuding he was an aide in the opening office.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuding he was an opening-office aide.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, noble titles were reduced by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi, ranks fell as usual.

sentences.zh: 義勰弟義雲，尚書騎兵郎中。

translations.literal: Yixie's younger brother Yiyun was an aide in the Cavalry Bureau of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Yiyun was a cavalry-bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 祖歸，官至建寧太守。

translations.literal: Zugui rose to governor of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Zugui became Jianning governor.

sentences.zh: 子義遠，武定中，平原太守。

translations.literal: His son Yiyuan in Wuding was Pingyuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yiyuan was Pingyuan governor in Wuding.

sentences.zh: 義遠弟義顯、義儁，性並豪率。

translations.literal: Yiyuan's younger brothers Yixian and Yijun were both bold and forthright by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers Yixian and Yijun were both brash.

sentences.zh: 天平已後，蕭衍使人還往，經歷兗城，前後州將以義儁兄弟善營鮭膳，器物鮮華，常兼長史，接宴賓客。

translations.literal: After Tianping, Xiao Yan's envoys came and went, passing through Yan city; successive Yan governors, because the Yijun brothers were skilled at preparing salmon delicacies and their vessels were fresh and splendid, often made them concurrent chief clerks to receive and feast guests.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianping, Liang envoys passed Yan; governors used the brothers' famous feasts and made them chief clerks for banquets.

sentences.zh: 義顯，左將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Yixian was Left General and Palace Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Yixian was Left General and Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 義儁，歷司空主簿、兗州別駕而卒。

translations.literal: Yijun passed through Works chief clerk and Yan vice governor, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Yijun was Works chief clerk and Yan vice governor, then died.

sentences.zh: 祖旋，太尉行參軍、鎮遠將軍。

translations.literal: Zuxuan was a staff officer of the Grand Minister and General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: Zuxuan was Grand Minister staff officer and General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈都官尚書、齊兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Minister of Justice and governor of Qi and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Minister of Justice and Qi-Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 子義真，太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yizhen was a Grand Minister staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yizhen was a Grand Minister staff officer.

sentences.zh: 眾敬弟眾愛，隨兄歸國。

translations.literal: Zhongjing's younger brother Zhong'ai followed his brother in returning to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zhong'ai followed him to Wei.

sentences.zh: 以勳為第一客，賜爵鉅平侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was a chief guest and enfeoffed Marquis of Juping.
translations.idiomatic: Honored as chief guest, he was Marquis of Juping.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冠軍將軍、徐州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously General Who Champions the Army and Xu governor, posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously General Who Champions the Army and Xu governor, posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 子聞慰，字子安，有器幹。

translations.literal: His son Wenwei, courtesy name Zi'an, had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Son Wenwei, styled Zi'an, was capable.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: He inherited the title, reduced by precedent to baron.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited, lowered to baron.

sentences.zh: 拜泰山太守，入為尚書郎、本州中正，加威遠將軍。

translations.literal: He was made Taishan governor, entered as Secretariat Gentleman and home-province rectifier, with the additional title General Who Prestiges the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Taishan, then became secretariat gentleman, rectifier, and General Who Prestiges the Distance.

sentences.zh: 出為徐州平東府長史，帶彭城內史。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk of Xu's Pacifying-East headquarters, concurrent Pengcheng metropolitan governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was chief clerk at Xu's eastern headquarters with Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 永平中，遷中散大夫，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: In Yongping he was promoted to Scattered Cavalry Grandee with the additional title Dragon Agile General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping he became Scattered-Cavalry Grandee and Dragon Agile General.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，除清河內史，因以疾辭，復為龍驤、中散。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yan chang he was made metropolitan governor of Qinghe; because of illness he resigned and again became Dragon Agile General and Scattered Cavalry Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yan chang he took Qinghe, resigned ill, and returned to dragon-agile and scattered-cavalry ranks.

sentences.zh: 又試守廣平內史。

translations.literal: He was again tried as acting metropolitan governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He later acted as Guangping metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 正光初，相州刺史、中山王熙起兵謀誅元叉，聞慰斬其使，發兵拒之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang, Xiang governor Prince of Zhongshan Xi raised troops plotting to kill Yuan Cha; Wenwei beheaded his envoy and raised troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguang Prince Xi of Zhongshan rebelled against Yuan Cha; Wenwei killed his envoy and resisted.

sentences.zh: 在任寬謹，百姓愛附。

translations.literal: In office he was lenient and careful, and the people loved and attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled leniently and the people clung to him.

sentences.zh: 後叉以聞慰忠於己，遷持節、平東將軍、滄州刺史，甚有政績。

translations.literal: Later Cha, because Wenwei was loyal to him, transferred him Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, and Cang governor, with very fine administrative achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Cha later made him Bearer of the Staff, eastern conqueror, and Cang governor for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 後以本軍除散騎常侍、東道行臺，尋為都督、安樂王鑒軍司。

translations.literal: Later with his former army he was made Scattered-Cavalry Attendant and Eastern Route Commissioner; soon he was Commissioner and army secretary to Prince of Anle Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He became Scattered-Cavalry Attendant and eastern commissioner, then Jian's army secretary.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年春，徐州刺史元法僧反，聞慰與鑒攻之，為法僧所敗，奔還京師。
