translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiaochang, Xu governor Yuan Faseng rebelled; Wenwei with Jian attacked him, was defeated by Faseng, and fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang's spring Yuan Faseng rebelled; Wenwei and Jian were beaten and fled to court.

sentences.zh: 被劾，遇赦免。

translations.literal: He was impeached but met amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached, he was spared by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安東將軍、兗州刺史，伯如故，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, General Who Pacifies the East, and Yan governor, baron's title unchanged, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, eastern conqueror, and Yan governor, baron unchanged, posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子祖彥，字脩賢。

translations.literal: His son Zuyan, courtesy name Xiuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zuyan, styled Xiuxian.

sentences.zh: 涉獵書傳，風度閑雅，為時所知。

translations.literal: He ranged through books and histories, bearing was leisurely and elegant, and men of the time knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Well read, elegant in manner, widely known.

sentences.zh: 以侍御史為元法僧監軍。

translations.literal: As investigating censor he was monitor of the army for Yuan Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: As censor he monitored Yuan Faseng's army.

sentences.zh: 法僧反，逼祖彥南入，永安中，得還。

translations.literal: Faseng rebelled and forced Zuyan south; in Yong'an he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Faseng rebelled he was driven south but returned in Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 歷中書侍郎，襲爵鉅平伯，中軍將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He passed through Secretariat Attendant, inherited the Baron of Juping, General of the Central Army, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretariat attendant, Baron of Juping, Central Army general, and Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 天平四年卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianping year four at fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈都督兗濟二州諸軍事、征東將軍、尚書左僕射、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously Commander over military affairs in Yan and Ji, General Who Conquers the East, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, and Yan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously commander of Yan and Ji, eastern conqueror, left vice minister, and Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 祖彥弟哲，永安末，祕書郎。

translations.literal: Zuyan's younger brother Zhe at the end of Yong'an was a Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhe was a secretariat gentleman in late Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 諸畢當朝，不乏榮貴，但幃薄不修，為時所鄙。

translations.literal: The Bi clan in court did not lack glory and rank, but their curtains were not kept in order and men of the time despised them.
translations.idiomatic: The Bis at court were rich in honors but lax in morals and despised.

sentences.zh: 申纂者，本魏郡人，申鍾曾孫也。

translations.literal: Shen Zuan was originally a man of Wei Commandery, great-grandson of Shen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuan of Wei Commandery was Shen Zhong's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，太祖平中山，纂宗室南奔，家于濟陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi the Taizu pacified Zhongshan; Zuan's clan fled south and settled in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Zhongshan, the clan fled south to Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 及在無鹽，劉彧用為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When he was at Wuyan, Liu Yu employed him as Yan governor.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuyan Liu Yu made him Yan governor.

sentences.zh: 顯祖曰：「申纂既不識機，又不量力，進不能歸正朔，退不能還江南，守孤城於危亡之地，欲建功立節豈可得乎！」

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu said: "Shen Zuan neither understood the moment nor measured his strength. Advancing, he could not return to the legitimate calendar; retreating, he could not return south of the Yangzi. Guarding a lone city in a place of danger and ruin, how could he hope to establish merit and preserve integrity!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu said: "Shen Zuan neither understood the moment nor measured his strength. Advancing, he could not return to the legitimate calendar; retreating, he could not return south of the Yangzi. Guarding a lone city in a place of danger and ruin, how could he hope to establish merit and preserve integrity!"

sentences.zh: 纂既敗，子景義入國，太和中，為散員士、宋王劉昶國侍郎。

translations.literal: After Zuan was defeated, his son Jingyi entered the realm; in Taihe he was a scattered guardsman and aide in Prince of Song Liu Chang's state.
translations.idiomatic: After Zuan's fall son Jingyi came to Wei and in Taihe served Liu Chang's princedom.

sentences.zh: 景明初，試守濟陰郡、揚州車騎府錄事參軍、右司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he was tried as Jiyin governor, recorder of Yangzhou's Chariots-and-Cavalry headquarters, and right marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingming he tried Jiyin, Yangzhou records, and right marshal.

sentences.zh: 常珍奇者，汝南人也。

translations.literal: Chang Zhenqi was a man of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Zhenqi came from Runan.

sentences.zh: 為劉駿司州刺史，亦與薛安都等推立劉子勛。

translations.literal: He was Liu Jun's Si governor and also with Xue Andou and others enthroned Liu Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: He was Liu Jun's Si governor and backed Zixun with Andou.

sentences.zh: 子勛敗，遣使馳告長社鎮請降，顯祖遣殿中尚書元石為都將，率眾赴之。

translations.literal: When Zixun was defeated he sent envoys in haste to report to Changshe garrison requesting surrender; Emperor Xianzu sent Palace Masters of Writing Yuan Shi as chief commander with troops to go.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun's defeat he asked Changshe to surrender; Yuan Shi was sent with troops.

sentences.zh: 中書博士鄭羲參石軍事。

translations.literal: Secretariat Doctor Zheng Xi joined Shi's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Zheng Xi joined Shi's staff.

sentences.zh: 進至上蔡，珍奇率文武來迎，羲說石令徑入城，語在羲傳。

translations.literal: Advancing to Shangcai, Zhenqi led civil and military officials to welcome him; Xi urged Shi to enter the city directly—the account is in Xi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangcai Zhenqi welcomed them; Xi urged entering the city at once (see Xi's biography).

sentences.zh: 事定，以珍奇為持節、平南將軍、豫州刺史、河內公。

translations.literal: When settled, Zhenqi was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Yu governor, and Duke of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Bearer of the Staff, southern conqueror, Yu governor, and Duke of Henei.

sentences.zh: 珍奇表曰：「臣昔蒙劉氏生成之恩，感義亡身，志陳報答，遂與雍州刺史袁顗、豫州刺史殷琰等共唱大義，奉戴子勛，纂承彼曆。

translations.literal: Zhenqi memorialized: "Formerly I received from the Liu house the grace of life and nurture. Moved by righteousness to risk my life and intending to present repayment, I joined Yongzhou Governor Yuan Yi and Yuzhou Governor Yin Yan in proclaiming the great cause, supporting Zixun and continuing that calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenqi memorialized: "Formerly I received from the Liu house the grace of life and nurture. Moved by righteousness to risk my life and intending to present repayment, I joined Yongzhou Governor Yuan Yi and Yuzhou Governor Yin Yan in proclaiming the great cause, supporting Zixun and continuing that calendar.

sentences.zh: 大運未集，遂至分崩。

translations.literal: The great fortune did not come together, and so it fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: The great fortune did not come together, and so it fell apart.

sentences.zh: 而劉彧滔天，殺主篡立，蒼生殄悴，危於綴旒。

translations.literal: But Liu Yu’s crime reaches Heaven: he killed his lord and usurped the throne, and the common people are destroyed and wearied, in danger like pendant tassels.
translations.idiomatic: But Liu Yu’s crime reaches Heaven: he killed his lord and usurped the throne, and the common people are destroyed and wearied, in danger like pendant tassels.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下龍姿鳳儀，光格四表，凡在黔黎，延屬象魏。

translations.literal: I reverently think that Your Majesty has dragon bearing and phoenix majesty, with radiance reaching the four quarters; all black-haired people turn toward the imperial gates.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently think that Your Majesty has dragon bearing and phoenix majesty, with radiance reaching the four quarters; all black-haired people turn toward the imperial gates.

sentences.zh: 所願天地垂仁，亟圖南服，宜遣文檄，喻以吉凶。

translations.literal: What I hope is that Heaven and Earth will extend benevolence, quickly plan for the southern lands, and send documents explaining fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: What I hope is that Heaven and Earth will extend benevolence, quickly plan for the southern lands, and send documents explaining fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 使江東之地，離心草靡；

translations.literal: Let the lands east of the Yangzi lose heart and bend like grass;
translations.idiomatic: Let the lands east of the Yangzi lose heart and bend like grass;

sentences.zh: 荊雍九州，北面請吏。

translations.literal: let the nine provinces of Jing and Yong face north and request officials.
translations.idiomatic: let the nine provinces of Jing and Yong face north and request officials.

sentences.zh: 乞高臣官名，更遣雄將，秣馬五千，助臣經討，并賜威儀，震動江外。

translations.literal: I beg that you elevate my official title, dispatch another mighty general, feed five thousand horses, assist me in campaigning, and grant ceremonial authority to shake the lands beyond the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that you elevate my official title, dispatch another mighty general, feed five thousand horses, assist me in campaigning, and grant ceremonial authority to shake the lands beyond the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 長江已北，必可定矣。

translations.literal: North of the Yangzi can surely be settled.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yangzi can surely be settled.

sentences.zh: 臣雖不武，乞備前驅，進據之宜，更在處分。

translations.literal: Though I am not martial, I beg to serve as the vanguard; the proper way to advance and occupy can further await instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not martial, I beg to serve as the vanguard; the proper way to advance and occupy can further await instructions.

sentences.zh: 敢冒愚款，推誠上聞，機運可乘，實在茲日。」

translations.literal: I dare to present my foolish sincerity and report it with complete honesty. The turn of opportunity can be seized; truly it lies in this day."
translations.idiomatic: I dare to present my foolish sincerity and report it with complete honesty. The turn of opportunity can be seized; truly it lies in this day."

sentences.zh: 珍奇雖有虛表，而誠款未純。

translations.literal: Though Zhenqi had an empty memorial, his sincere intent was not pure.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was grand but his heart was not loyal.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，徵其子超，超母胡氏不欲超赴京師，密懷南叛。

translations.literal: After more than a year his son Chao was summoned; Chao's mother the Hu clan did not wish Chao to go to the capital and secretly harbored southern rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When son Chao was summoned, his mother Hu plotted south.

sentences.zh: 時汝徐未平，元石自出攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Ru and Xu were not yet pacified; Yuan Shi himself went out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Ru and Xu still rebelled; Yuan Shi campaigned.

sentences.zh: 珍奇乘虛於懸瓠反叛，燒城東門，斬三百餘人，虜掠上蔡、安城、平輿三縣居民，屯于灌水。

translations.literal: Zhenqi seized the chance to rebel at Xuancheng, burned the eastern gate, beheaded more than three hundred, carried off the people of Shangcai, Ancheng, and Pingyu, and camped on the Guan water.
translations.idiomatic: He rebelled at Xuancheng, burned the gate, slaughtered hundreds, and raided three counties.

sentences.zh: 石馳往討擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Shi galloped to strike and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi routed him in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 會日闇，放火燒其營，珍奇乃匹馬逃免。

translations.literal: As night fell he set fire and burned their camp; Zhenqi alone on horseback escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he burned the camp; Zhenqi fled alone.

sentences.zh: 其子超走到苦城，為人所殺。

translations.literal: His son Chao fled to Kucheng and was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chao was killed fleeing to Kucheng.

sentences.zh: 小子沙彌囚送京師，刑為閹人。

translations.literal: The younger son Shamini was bound and sent to the capital and punished by castration.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Shamini was castrated as a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 沈文秀，字仲遠，吳興武康人。

translations.literal: Shen Wenxiu, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu of Wukang in Wuxing, styled Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 伯父慶之，劉駿司空公。

translations.literal: His uncle Qingzhi was Duke of the Excellency of Works under Liu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Qingzhi was Liu Jun's Works duke.

sentences.zh: 文秀初為郡主簿，稍遷建威將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Wenxiu first was the commandery chief clerk, then gradually rose to General Who Establishes Might and Qing governor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as commandery clerk, then became mighty-establisher and Qing governor.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，劉子業為其叔彧所殺，文秀遂與諸州推立劉子勛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, Liu Ziye was killed by his uncle Yu; Wenxiu then with the provinces enthroned Liu Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping year six Ziye was killed; Wenxiu backed Zixun.

sentences.zh: 及子勛敗，皇興初，文秀與崔道固俱以州降，請師應接，顯祖遣平東將軍長孫陵等率騎赴之。

translations.literal: When Zixun was defeated, at the beginning of Huangxing Wenxiu with Cui Daogu both surrendered the province and begged troops; Emperor Xianzu sent General Who Pacifies the East Changsun Ling and others with cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun's fall he and Cui Daogu surrendered; Ling was sent with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 會劉彧遣文秀弟文炳來喻之，文秀復歸於彧，彧以文秀為輔國將軍、刺史如故。

translations.literal: But Liu Yu sent Wenxiu's younger brother Wenbing to persuade him; Wenxiu returned to Yu, and Yu made him General Who Assists the State, governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's brother Wenbing turned him back; Yu restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 後慕容白曜既克升城，引軍向歷下，白曜復遣陵等率萬餘人長驅至東陽。

translations.literal: Later Murong Baiyao having taken Shengcheng led his army toward Lixia; Baiyao again sent Ling and others with more than ten thousand men in long drive to Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Baiyao took Shengcheng he sent Ling with ten thousand to Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 文秀始欲降，以軍人虜掠，遂有悔心，乃嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Wenxiu at first wished to surrender, but because the soldiers plundered he had second thoughts and then walled the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to surrender until soldiers looted; then he held the city.

sentences.zh: 陵乃引師軍於清西。

translations.literal: Ling then drew his army on the west of the Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Ling camped west of the Qing.

sentences.zh: 白曜既下歷城，乃率大眾并力攻討，長圍數匝，自夏至春始克。

translations.literal: Baiyao having taken Lixia then led the great host with combined strength to attack; a long siege of many circuits from summer to spring before it fell.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao took Lixia, then besieged Dongyang from summer to spring.

sentences.zh: 文秀取所持節，衣冠儼然，坐於齋內。

translations.literal: Wenxiu took the staff he held, robes and hat dignified, and sat within his study.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in full regalia with his staff in his study.

sentences.zh: 亂兵入，曰：「文秀何在？」

translations.literal: Rebel soldiers entered and asked: "Where is Wenxiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Rebel soldiers entered and asked: "Where is Wenxiu?"

sentences.zh: 文秀厲聲曰：「身是！」

translations.literal: Wenxiu said in a stern voice: "I am he!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered sternly: "I am he!"

sentences.zh: 執而裸送于白曜。

translations.literal: They seized him and stripped him and sent him to Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped him and sent him to Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 左右令拜，文秀曰：「各二國大臣，無相拜之禮。」

translations.literal: Those around him ordered him to bow. Wenxiu said: "We are each great ministers of two states; there is no ritual of bowing to one another."
translations.idiomatic: Those around him ordered him to bow. Wenxiu said: "We are each great ministers of two states; there is no ritual of bowing to one another."

sentences.zh: 白曜忿之，乃至撾撻。

translations.literal: Baiyao was angry and even beat him with clubs.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 後還其衣，為之設饌，遂與長史房天樂、司馬沈嵩等鎖送京師。

translations.literal: Later they returned his clothes, set out food for him, and with Chief Clerk Fang Tianle and Marshal Shen Song and others sent him in chains to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later clothed and fed, he was chained to the capital with Fang Tianle and Shen Song.

sentences.zh: 面縛數罪，宥死，待為下客，給以粗衣蔬食。

translations.literal: His face bound, several crimes were listed; death was spared and he was kept as a lower guest with coarse clothes and plain food.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned but spared, he was a low guest in coarse dress.

sentences.zh: 顯祖重其節義，稍亦加禮之，拜為外都下大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu valued his integrity and gradually added ceremony, making him Outer Court Lower Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu honored his loyalty and made him outer-court lower grandee.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，遷外都大官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was moved to Outer Court Grand Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year three he became outer grand provisioner.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉文秀忠於其國，賜絹綵二百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised Wenxiu's loyalty to his state and granted two hundred bolts of silk brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised his loyalty and gave silk.

sentences.zh: 後為南征都將，臨發，賜以戎服。

translations.literal: Later as southern campaign chief commander, on setting out he was granted military dress.
translations.idiomatic: As southern commander he received military dress on departure.

sentences.zh: 尋除持節、平南將軍、懷州刺史，假吳郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, Huai governor, and Acting Duke of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bearer of the Staff, southern conqueror, Huai governor, Acting Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 是時河南富饒，人好奉遺，文秀一無所納，卒守清貧。

translations.literal: At that time Henan was rich; people loved to offer gifts—Wenxiu accepted nothing and to the end kept clear poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Rich Henan offered gifts; he took none and stayed poor.

sentences.zh: 然為政寬緩，不能禁止盜賊；

translations.literal: Yet his governance was lenient and slow and could not forbid bandits;
translations.idiomatic: He was lenient and could not stop bandits;

sentences.zh: 而大興水田，於公私頗有利益。

translations.literal: but he greatly opened paddy fields, to public and private considerable benefit.
translations.idiomatic: yet he opened paddies to great public benefit.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，年六十一，卒。

translations.literal: Several years in the province, aged sixty-one, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 子保沖，太和中，奉朝請、大將軍宋王外兵參軍，後為南徐州冠軍長史。

translations.literal: His son Baochong in Taihe was Court Gentleman and outer military aide to the great general Prince of Song, later southern Xu champion chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Son Baochong was court gentleman and Song prince aide, later southern Xu chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，坐援漣口退敗，有司處之死刑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, for defeat and retreat at Lian mouth, the authorities sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he was sentenced to death for defeat at Lian mouth.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔曰：「保沖，文秀之子，可特原命，配洛陽作部終身。」

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an edict: "Baochong is Wenxiu’s son; his life may specially be spared, and he shall be assigned for life to the Luoyang workshops."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu issued an edict: "Baochong is Wenxiu’s son; his life may specially be spared, and he shall be assigned for life to the Luoyang workshops."

sentences.zh: 既而獲免。

translations.literal: Afterward he was also pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was later pardoned.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，卒於下邳太守。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time he died as Xiapi governor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he died as Xiapi governor.

sentences.zh: 房天樂者，清河人，滑稽多智。

translations.literal: Fang Tianle was a man of Qinghe, witty and very clever.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Tianle of Qinghe was witty and clever.

sentences.zh: 先為青州別駕，文秀拔為長史，督齊郡，州府之事，一以委之。

translations.literal: First he was Qing vice governor; Wenxiu pulled him up as chief clerk supervising Qi commandery, and all provincial affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu made him chief clerk over Qi and trusted all affairs to him.

sentences.zh: 卒于京師。

translations.literal: He died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died at court.

sentences.zh: 弟子嘉慶，漁陽太守。

translations.literal: His younger brother's son Jiaqing was Yuyang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Jiaqing was Yuyang governor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶從弟瑚璉，長廣太守。

translations.literal: Jiaqing's cousin from the father's line Hulian was Changguang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Hulian was Changguang governor.

sentences.zh: 文秀族子嵩，聰敏有筆札。

translations.literal: Wenxiu's clansman Song was clever and had a hand for writing.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Song was clever with writing.

sentences.zh: 文秀以為司馬，甚器任之。

translations.literal: Wenxiu made him marshal and greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu made him marshal and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 隨文秀至懷州。

translations.literal: He followed Wenxiu to Huai Province.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wenxiu to Huai.

sentences.zh: 文秀卒後，依宋王劉昶。

translations.literal: After Wenxiu died he relied on Prince of Song Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenxiu's death he served Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶遇之無禮，憂愧飢寒，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Chang treated him without courtesy; grieved, ashamed, hungry and cold, he died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Chang treated him poorly; he died in misery.

sentences.zh: 文秀族子陵，字道通。

translations.literal: Wenxiu's clansman Ling, courtesy name Daotong.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman Ling, styled Daotong.

sentences.zh: 太和十八年，高祖南伐，陵攜族孫智度歸降，引見於行宮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Taihe, when Gaozu campaigned south, Ling brought his clan grandson Zhidu in surrender and was received at the mobile palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year eighteen Ling surrendered with Zhidu at the mobile palace.

sentences.zh: 陵姿質妍偉，辭氣辯暢，高祖奇之，禮遇亞於王肅，授前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Ling's bearing was handsome, his speech eloquent; Gaozu marveled and treated him next below Wang Su, appointing Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and eloquent, Gaozu favored him below Wang Su and made him Forward General.

sentences.zh: 後監南徐州諸軍事、中壘將軍、南徐州刺史，尋假節、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Later he supervised southern Xu military affairs, General of the Central Rampart, southern Xu governor, soon Acting Bearer of the Staff and Dragon Agile General.
translations.idiomatic: He governed southern Xu, then held the staff as Dragon Agile General.

sentences.zh: 二十二年秋，進持節、冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-second year he advanced to Bearer of the Staff and General Who Champions the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year twenty-two he became Bearer of the Staff and champion general.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，陵陰有叛心，長史趙儼密言于朝廷，尚書令王肅深保明之，切責儼。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Ling secretly had rebellious intent; Chief Clerk Zhao Yan secretly reported to court; Minister Wang Su deeply vouched for him and sharply rebuked Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's death Ling plotted revolt; Yan reported but Su defended him and rebuked Yan.

sentences.zh: 既而果叛，殺數十人，驅掠城中男女百餘口，夜走南入。

translations.literal: Soon he truly rebelled, killed several tens, drove off and seized more than a hundred men and women in the city, and fled south by night.
translations.idiomatic: He rebelled, killed dozens, seized townsfolk, and fled south.

sentences.zh: 智度於彭城知之，從清中單舸奔陵，為下邳戍人所射殺。

translations.literal: Zhidu at Pengcheng learned of it and in a single boat from the Qing middle course rushed to Ling, but was shot and killed by Xiapi garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidu tried to join him and was killed by Xiapi garrison.

sentences.zh: 張讜，字處言，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dang, courtesy name Chuyan, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dang of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, styled Chuyan.

sentences.zh: 六世祖名犯顯祖諱，晉長秋卿。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor's name violated Emperor Xianzu's taboo; he was Jin Director of the Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: A sixth-generation ancestor's name tabooed Xianzu; he was Jin Director of Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 父華，為慕容超左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Hua was Left Vice Minister under Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Father Hua was Chao's left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 讜仕劉駿，歷給事中、泰山太守、青冀二州輔國府長史，帶魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Dang served Liu Jun, passing through Gentleman at the Palace Gate, Taishan governor, chief clerk of Qing-Ji auxiliary state, and concurrent Wei governor.
translations.idiomatic: Dang served Liu Jun as palace gentleman, Taishan and Wei governor, and Qing-Ji chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉彧之立，遙授冠軍將軍、東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At Liu Yu's enthronement he was remotely made General Who Champions the Army and eastern Xu governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu took power, Dang was named champion general and eastern Xu governor.

sentences.zh: 及革徐兗，讜乃歸順於尉元。

translations.literal: When Xu and Yan were reformed, Dang then submitted to Wei Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu and Yan changed hands, he submitted to Wei Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元亦表授冠軍、東徐州刺史，遣中書侍郎高閭與讜對為刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan also appointed him champion and eastern Xu governor and sent Secretariat Attendant Gao Lu to pair with Dang as governors.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan paired him as governor with Gao Lu.

sentences.zh: 後至京師，禮遇亞於薛、畢，以勳賜爵平陸侯，加平遠將軍。

translations.literal: Later reaching the capital, his courtesy was next below Xue and Bi; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pinglu and made General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: At court he ranked below Xue and Bi and was Marquis of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 讜性開通，篤於撫恤，青齊之士，雖疏族末姻，咸相敬視。

translations.literal: Dang's nature was open and penetrating, earnest in comfort and relief; Qing-Qi gentlemen, though distant kin or remote affines, all respected and regarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Open and caring, he won Qing and Qi gentry even of distant kin.

sentences.zh: 李敷、李訢等寵要勢家，亦推懷陳款，無所顧避。

translations.literal: Li Fu, Li Xin, and other powerful favorites also opened their hearts in sincerity without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: Even favorites Li Fu and Li Xin dealt with him openly.

sentences.zh: 畢眾敬等皆敬重之，高允之徒亦相器待。

translations.literal: Bi Zhongjing and the rest all respected him; Gao Yun and such also valued and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing and Gao Yun esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 延興四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yanxing year four.

sentences.zh: 贈平南將軍、青州刺史，諡康侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously General Who Pacifies the South and Qing governor, posthumous name Kang Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously southern conqueror and Qing governor, posthumous Kang.

sentences.zh: 子敬伯，求致父喪，出葬冀州清河舊墓，久不被許，停柩在家積五六年。

translations.literal: His son Jingbo begged to bring his father's coffin out for burial in Qinghe's old tomb in Ji Province; long disallowed, the bier stayed at home five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: Son Jingbo fought years to bury him in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 第四子敬叔，先在徐州，初聞父喪，不欲奔赴，而規南叛，為徐州所勒送。

translations.literal: The fourth son Jingshu was first at Xu; on hearing of the father's death he would not hurry to the funeral but plotted southern rebellion and was compelled by Xu to be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth son Jingshu at Xu plotted south instead of mourning and was sent under guard.

sentences.zh: 至乃自理，後得襲父爵。

translations.literal: When he arrived he explained himself and later could inherit his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He explained himself and inherited.

sentences.zh: 敬伯，自以隨父歸國之功，賜爵昌安侯，出為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Jingbo, for the merit of following his father in returning to the realm, was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an and went out as Leling governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo was Marquis of Chang'an and Leling governor for the family's surrender.

sentences.zh: 敬叔，武邑太守。

translations.literal: Jingshu was Wuyi governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshu was Wuyi governor.

sentences.zh: 父喪得葬舊墓，還屬清河。

translations.literal: When the father's burial in the old tomb was granted, he returned to Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: After burial was allowed he returned to Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 初，讜兄弟十人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dang had ten brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Dang had ten brothers.

sentences.zh: 兄忠，字處順，在南為合鄉令。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhong, courtesy name Chushun, in the south was magistrate of Hexiang.
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Zhong, styled Chushun, was Hexiang magistrate in the south.

sentences.zh: 世祖南征，忠歸降，賜爵新昌男，拜新興太守，卒官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu campaigned south, Zhong surrendered and was enfeoffed Baron of Xinchang and made Xinxing governor, dying in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's southern campaign brought Zhong's surrender; he died Xinxing governor.

sentences.zh: 贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously Ji governor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Ji governor.

sentences.zh: 初，讜妻皇甫氏被掠，賜中官為婢，皇甫遂乃詐癡，不能梳沐。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dang's wife the Huangfu clan was seized and given to a palace eunuch as maid; Huangfu then feigned madness and could not comb or wash.
translations.idiomatic: Wife Huangfu was taken as a eunuch's maid and feigned madness.

sentences.zh: 後讜為劉駿冀州長史，因貨千餘匹購求皇甫。

translations.literal: Later when Dang was Liu Jun's Ji chief clerk, he bought Huangfu back with more than a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Jun's Ji chief clerk he bought her back for a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 高宗怪其納財之多也，引見之，時皇甫年垂六十矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong wondered at the great payment and summoned her; Huangfu was then nearly sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong wondered at the price; she was nearly sixty.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「南人奇好，能重室家之義，此老母復何所任，乃能如此致費也。」

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "Southerners are wonderfully devoted, able to value the duty between husband and wife. What use can this old mother still be, that he could spend so much on her?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong said: "Southerners are wonderfully devoted, able to value the duty between husband and wife. What use can this old mother still be, that he could spend so much on her?"

sentences.zh: 皇甫氏歸，讜令諸妾境上奉迎。

translations.literal: Huangfu returned; Dang had the concubines meet her at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu returned; concubines met her at the border.

sentences.zh: 數年卒，卒後十年而讜入國。

translations.literal: Several years later she died; ten years after her death Dang entered the realm.
translations.idiomatic: She died; Dang came to Wei ten years later.

sentences.zh: 讜兄子安世，正始中，自梁漢同夏侯道遷歸款。

translations.literal: Dang's elder brother's son Anshi in Zhengshi from Liang-Han with Xiahou Daogian came over in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Anshi surrendered with Xiahou Daogian in Zhengshi.

sentences.zh: 為客積年，出為東河間太守，卒官。

translations.literal: As a guest for years he went out as Donghejian governor and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A guest for years, he died Donghejian governor.

sentences.zh: 元茂，[6]為信都令，遷冀州治中。

translations.literal: Yuanmao[6] was magistrate of Xindu and moved to Ji chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmao[6] was Xindu magistrate then Ji chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 元茂弟子讓，洛州安西府長史、都水使者。

translations.literal: Yuanmao's younger brother's son Rang was Luozhou Anxi headquarters chief clerk and Director of Waters.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Rang was Luozhou chief clerk and Director of Waters.

sentences.zh: 田益宗，光城蠻也。

translations.literal: Tian Yizong was a Guangcheng Man.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizong was a Guangcheng barbarian.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，雄果有將略，貌狀舉止，有異常蠻。

translations.literal: Eight feet tall, fierce and fruit-bearing with military strategy, his appearance and bearing quite unlike ordinary barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet, fierce, soldierly, unlike common Man.

sentences.zh: 世為四山蠻帥，受制於蕭賾。

translations.literal: For generations chief of the Four Mountains Man, subject to Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: His line ruled Four Mountains Man under Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，遣使張超奉表歸款。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, envoy Zhang Chao offered a submission of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year seventeen Zhang Chao submitted allegiance.

sentences.zh: 十九年，拜員外散騎常侍、都督光城弋陽汝南新蔡宋安五郡諸軍事、冠軍將軍、南司州刺史；

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was made Outer Palace Attendant in the Scattered Cavalry, Commander over Guangcheng, Yiyang, Runan, Xincai, Song'an military affairs, General Who Champions the Army, and southern Si governor;
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen he became scattered-cavalry attendant, southern Si commander, and champion general;

sentences.zh: 光城縣開國伯，食蠻邑一千戶；

translations.literal: Baron of Guangcheng county with a Man fief of one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Baron of Guangcheng at a thousand Man households;

sentences.zh: 所統守宰，任其銓置。

translations.literal: the prefects and magistrates he ruled he appointed at will.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed his own officials.

sentences.zh: 後以益宗既渡淮北，不可仍為司州，乃於新蔡立東豫州，以益宗為刺史。

translations.literal: Later because Yizong had crossed north of the Huai and could not still be Si, Eastern Yu was established at Xincai with Yizong as governor.
translations.idiomatic: After he crossed the Huai, Eastern Yu was created at Xincai for him.

sentences.zh: 尋改封安昌縣伯，食實邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon his fief was changed to Baron of Anchang with five hundred substantive households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief became Anchang at five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year his title advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he became General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 景明初，蕭衍遣軍主吳子陽率眾寇三關。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Xiao Yan's army commander Wu Ziyang led a host to raid the three passes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingming Wu Ziyang raided the three passes.

sentences.zh: [7]益宗遣光城太守梅興之步騎四千，進至陰山關南八十餘里，據長風城，逆擊子陽，大破之，斬獲千餘級。

translations.literal: [7] Yizong sent Guangcheng governor Mei Xingzhi with four thousand foot and horse to within eighty li south of Yinshan Pass, seized Changfeng city, and met Ziyang head-on, routing him and taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: [7] He sent Mei Xingzhi with four thousand to Changfeng and routed Wu Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍建寧太守黃天賜築城赤亭，復遣其將黃公賞屯於漴城，與長風相持。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Jianning governor Huang Tiansi built a wall at Chiting; he again sent his general Huang Gongshang to camp at Chong city, stalemate with Changfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tiansi built at Chiting and posted Huang Gongshang at Chong.

sentences.zh: 益宗命安蠻太守梅景秀為之掎角擊討，破天賜等，斬首數百，獲其二城。

translations.literal: Yizong ordered Pacify-the-Man governor Mei Jingxiu to strike in pincers and broke Tiansi and the rest, taking several hundred heads and their two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Jingxiu pincered and took both cities.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：「臣聞機之所在，聖賢弗之疑；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that when opportunity lies before them, sages and worthies do not doubt it;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that when opportunity lies before them, sages and worthies do not doubt it;

sentences.zh: 兼弱攻昧，前王莫之捨。

translations.literal: to annex the weak and attack the benighted was something former kings never abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: to annex the weak and attack the benighted was something former kings never abandoned.

sentences.zh: 皆拯羣生於湯炭，盛武功於方來。

translations.literal: They all rescued the multitudes from boiling water and fire, and made martial achievement flourish for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: They all rescued the multitudes from boiling water and fire, and made martial achievement flourish for later ages.

sentences.zh: 然霜葉將淪，非勁飈無以速其籜；

translations.literal: But when frost-struck leaves are about to fall, without a strong wind there is no way to hasten their shedding;
translations.idiomatic: But when frost-struck leaves are about to fall, without a strong wind there is no way to hasten their shedding;

sentences.zh: 天之所棄，非假手無以殲其人。

translations.literal: when Heaven has abandoned someone, without borrowing another hand there is no way to destroy that person.
translations.idiomatic: when Heaven has abandoned someone, without borrowing another hand there is no way to destroy that person.

sentences.zh: 竊惟蕭衍亂常，[8]君臣交爭，江外州鎮，中分為兩，東西抗峙，已淹歲時。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Xiao Yan has disordered the norms; ruler and ministers contend with each other, and the provinces and garrisons beyond the Yangzi are divided into two, standing against each other east and west, already for years.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Xiao Yan has disordered the norms; ruler and ministers contend with each other, and the provinces and garrisons beyond the Yangzi are divided into two, standing against each other east and west, already for years.

sentences.zh: 民庶窮於轉輸，甲兵疲於戰鬬，事救於目前，力盡於麾下。

translations.literal: The common people are exhausted by transport duties, and the armored troops are worn out by battle; their affairs are saved only for the moment, and their strength is spent beneath the banners.
translations.idiomatic: The common people are exhausted by transport duties, and the armored troops are worn out by battle; their affairs are saved only for the moment, and their strength is spent beneath the banners.

sentences.zh: 無暇外維州鎮，[9]綱紀庶方，藩城棊立，孤存而已。

translations.literal: They have no leisure to maintain the outer provinces and garrisons or order the many regions; their walled towns stand like chess pieces, merely surviving alone.
translations.idiomatic: They have no leisure to maintain the outer provinces and garrisons or order the many regions; their walled towns stand like chess pieces, merely surviving alone.

sentences.zh: 不乘機電掃，廓彼蠻疆，恐後之經略，未易於此。

translations.literal: If we do not seize the opportunity to sweep them away like lightning and clear that barbarian frontier, I fear later planning will not be easier than this.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not seize the opportunity to sweep them away like lightning and clear that barbarian frontier, I fear later planning will not be easier than this.

sentences.zh: 且壽春雖平，三面仍梗，鎮守之宜，實須豫設。

translations.literal: Moreover, although Shouchun has been pacified, three sides remain obstructed; the proper arrangements for garrison defense truly must be made in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, although Shouchun has been pacified, three sides remain obstructed; the proper arrangements for garrison defense truly must be made in advance.

sentences.zh: 義陽差近淮源，利涉津要，朝廷行師，必由此道。

translations.literal: Yiyang is somewhat near the Huai source and controls important crossings; when the court sends armies, they must pass by this route.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang is somewhat near the Huai source and controls important crossings; when the court sends armies, they must pass by this route.

sentences.zh: 若江南一平，有事淮外，須乘夏水汎長，列舟長淮。

translations.literal: If Jiangnan is once pacified and there is business beyond the Huai, we must take advantage of the summer floodwaters, array boats along the long Huai,
translations.idiomatic: If Jiangnan is once pacified and there is business beyond the Huai, we must take advantage of the summer floodwaters, array boats along the long Huai,

sentences.zh: 師赴壽春，須從義陽之北，便是居我喉要，在慮彌深。

translations.literal: and when the army goes to Shouchun it must pass north of Yiyang. This is precisely our throat, and the concern is all the deeper.
translations.idiomatic: and when the army goes to Shouchun it must pass north of Yiyang. This is precisely our throat, and the concern is all the deeper.

sentences.zh: 義陽之滅，今實時矣。

translations.literal: Now is truly the time to destroy Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Now is truly the time to destroy Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 度彼眾不過須精卒一萬二千。

translations.literal: I estimate that against their forces no more than twelve thousand elite soldiers are needed.
translations.idiomatic: I estimate that against their forces no more than twelve thousand elite soldiers are needed.

sentences.zh: 然行師之法，貴張形勢。

translations.literal: Yet in the method of moving armies, what matters is displaying power.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the method of moving armies, what matters is displaying power.

sentences.zh: 請使兩荊之眾西擬隨雍，揚州之卒頓于建安，得捍三關之援；

translations.literal: I request that the troops of the two Jing regions feint west toward Sui and Yong, and that the soldiers of Yangzhou halt at Jian’an, so as to block aid from the three passes;
translations.idiomatic: I request that the troops of the two Jing regions feint west toward Sui and Yong, and that the soldiers of Yangzhou halt at Jian’an, so as to block aid from the three passes;

sentences.zh: 然後二豫之軍直據南關，對抗延頭。

translations.literal: after that, the armies of the two Yu regions should directly occupy the southern pass and face Yantou.
translations.idiomatic: after that, the armies of the two Yu regions should directly occupy the southern pass and face Yantou.

sentences.zh: 遣一都督總諸軍節度，季冬進師，迄于春末，弗過十旬，克之必矣！」

translations.literal: Send one commander-in-chief to oversee the command of all the armies, advance in late winter, and by the end of spring, in no more than one hundred days, it will certainly be taken!"
translations.idiomatic: Send one commander-in-chief to oversee the command of all the armies, advance in late winter, and by the end of spring, in no more than one hundred days, it will certainly be taken!"

sentences.zh: 世宗納之，遣鎮南元英攻義陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong accepted it and sent Pacify-the-South Yuan Ying to attack Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Yuan Ying against Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 益宗遣其息魯生領步騎八千，斷賊粮運，并焚其鈞城積聚。

translations.literal: Yizong sent his son Lusheng leading eight thousand foot and horse to cut the bandits' grain transport and burn their stock at Jun city.
translations.idiomatic: Son Lusheng cut enemy grain and burned Jun stores.

sentences.zh: 衍戍主趙文舉率眾拒戰，魯生破之，獲文舉及小將胡建興、古皓、莊元仲等，斬五千餘級，溺死千五百人，倉米運舟焚燒蕩盡。

translations.literal: Yan garrison commander Zhao Wenju led a host to resist; Lusheng broke them, capturing Wenju and the lieutenants Hu Jianxing, Gu Hao, Zhuang Yuanchong and others, beheading more than five thousand, drowning fifteen hundred, grain boats burned clean.
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng beat Zhao Wenju, took five thousand heads, burned grain boats.

sentences.zh: 後賊寧朔將軍楊僧遠率眾二千，寇逼蒙籠，益宗命魯生與戍主奇道顯逆擊破之，追奔十里，俘斬千餘。

translations.literal: Later the bandit General Who Pacifies the North Yang Sengyuan led two thousand to press Menglong; Yizong ordered Lusheng and garrison commander Qi Daoxian to meet and rout them, pursuing ten li and taking more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Yang Sengyuan at Menglong.

sentences.zh: 進號平南將軍。

translations.literal: His title advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 又詔益宗率其部曲并州鎮文武，與假節、征虜將軍、太僕少卿宇文福綏防蠻楚，加安南將軍，增封一百戶，賜帛二千匹。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Yizong to lead his tribal troops with provincial and garrison civil and military officials together with Acting Bearer of the Staff, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Yuwen Fu to soothe and defend the Man of Chu, with the added title General Who Pacifies the South, fief increased by one hundred households, silk two thousand bolts granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Yuwen Fu to guard the Man frontier, added rank and silk.

sentences.zh: 白早生反於豫州，詔益宗曰：「懸瓠要藩，密邇崧潁，南疆之重，所寄不輕。

translations.literal: When Bai Zaosheng rebelled in Yuzhou, an edict to Yizong said: "Xuancheng is an important border stronghold, close to Song and Ying; the weight of the southern frontier entrusted to it is not light.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Zaosheng rebelled in Yuzhou, an edict to Yizong said: "Xuancheng is an important border stronghold, close to Song and Ying; the weight of the southern frontier entrusted to it is not light.

sentences.zh: 而羣小猖狂，忽構釁逆，殺害鎮主，規成反叛。

translations.literal: Yet petty men have run wild and suddenly created rebellion, killing the garrison commander and planning to complete their revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men have run wild and suddenly created rebellion, killing the garrison commander and planning to complete their revolt.

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可容。

translations.literal: If this can be endured, what cannot be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be endured, what cannot be tolerated?

sentences.zh: 即遣尚書邢巒總精騎五萬，星馳電驅；

translations.literal: We have already dispatched Minister Xing Luan to command fifty thousand elite cavalry, racing like stars and driving like lightning;
translations.idiomatic: We have already dispatched Minister Xing Luan to command fifty thousand elite cavalry, racing like stars and driving like lightning;

sentences.zh: 征南將軍、中山王英統馬步七萬，絡繹繼發。

translations.literal: General Who Campaigns South, Prince Ying of Zhongshan, commands seventy thousand horse and foot, following in continuous succession.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Campaigns South, Prince Ying of Zhongshan, commands seventy thousand horse and foot, following in continuous succession.

sentences.zh: 量此蟻寇唯當逃奔。

translations.literal: Measured against this ant-like banditry, they can only flee.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against this ant-like banditry, they can only flee.

sentences.zh: 知將軍志翦犲狼，以清邊境，節義慷慨，良在可嘉，非蹇蹇之至，何以能爾？

translations.literal: I know that the general’s resolve is to cut down jackals and wolves and clear the border; your integrity and righteousness are impassioned and truly praiseworthy. Without utmost devotion, how could this be so?
translations.idiomatic: I know that the general’s resolve is to cut down jackals and wolves and clear the border; your integrity and righteousness are impassioned and truly praiseworthy. Without utmost devotion, how could this be so?

sentences.zh: 深戢誠款，方相委託。

translations.literal: I deeply treasure your sincere loyalty and am about to entrust matters to you.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply treasure your sincere loyalty and am about to entrust matters to you.

sentences.zh: 故遣中書舍人趙文相具宣朕懷，往還之規，口別指授，便可善盡算略，隨宜追掩，勿令此豎得有竄逸。

translations.literal: Therefore I send Secretariat Drafter Zhao Wenxiang to fully proclaim my thoughts. As for the plan for going and returning, he will separately instruct you orally; you may then exhaust your calculations, pursue and strike as circumstances require, and not let these wretches escape.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I send Secretariat Drafter Zhao Wenxiang to fully proclaim my thoughts. As for the plan for going and returning, he will separately instruct you orally; you may then exhaust your calculations, pursue and strike as circumstances require, and not let these wretches escape.

sentences.zh: 遲近清盪，更有別旨。」

translations.literal: When the cleansing is nearly complete, there will be a separate command."
translations.idiomatic: When the cleansing is nearly complete, there will be a separate command."

sentences.zh: 時自樂口已南，郢豫二州諸城皆沒於賊，唯有義陽而已。

translations.literal: From Lekou south, Ying and Yu commandery cities all fell to bandits; only Yiyang remained.
translations.idiomatic: South of Lekou only Yiyang held.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍招益宗以車騎大將軍、開府、儀同三司、五千戶郡公。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan recruited Yizong with General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Opening Office, Three Excellencies honors, and Duke of a five-thousand-household commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan offered him chariots general, opening office, and a duchy.

sentences.zh: 當時安危，在益宗去就，而益宗守節不移。

translations.literal: At that time safety and peril hung on whether Yizong would stay or go, yet Yizong held his integrity and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The realm's fate hung on him; he did not move.

sentences.zh: 郢豫克平，益宗之力也。

translations.literal: When Ying and Yu were pacified, it was Yizong's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ying-Yu's recovery was his doing.

sentences.zh: 益宗年稍衰老，聚斂無厭，兵民患其侵擾。

translations.literal: Yizong gradually aged and amassed without end; soldiers and people resented his exactions.
translations.idiomatic: He aged and grew greedy; troops and people resented him.

sentences.zh: 諸子及孫競規賄貨，部內苦之，咸言欲叛。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons competed for bribes; within the commandery they suffered and all said he would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Kin took bribes; the province said he would rebel.

sentences.zh: 世宗深亦慮焉，乃遣中書舍人劉桃符宣旨慰喻，庶以安之。

translations.literal: The court also worried; it sent Secretariat Retainer Liu Taofu with an edict of comfort, hoping thereby to settle him.
translations.idiomatic: Court sent Liu Taofu to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 桃符還，啟益宗侵掠之狀。

translations.literal: Taofu returned and reported Yizong's predations.
translations.idiomatic: Taofu reported his extortion.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔之曰：「風聞卿息魯生淮南貪暴，擾亂細民，又橫殺梅伏生，為爾不已，損卿誠效。

translations.literal: Shizong issued an edict to him, saying: "I have heard that your son Lusheng is greedy and violent in Huainan, disturbing the common people and also wantonly killing Mei Fusheng. If this goes on without stopping, it will damage your sincere service.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong issued an edict to him, saying: "I have heard that your son Lusheng is greedy and violent in Huainan, disturbing the common people and also wantonly killing Mei Fusheng. If this goes on without stopping, it will damage your sincere service.

sentences.zh: 可令魯生與使赴闕，當加任使。

translations.literal: You may order Lusheng to come to court with the envoy, and he will be given an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: You may order Lusheng to come to court with the envoy, and he will be given an appointment.

sentences.zh: 如欲外祿，便授中畿一郡。」

translations.literal: If he wants an outside salary, he will be granted one commandery in the central region."
translations.idiomatic: If he wants an outside salary, he will be granted one commandery in the central region."

sentences.zh: 魯生久未至。

translations.literal: Lusheng long did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Lusheng did not come.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，詔曰：「益宗先朝耆艾，服勤邊境，不可以地須其人，遂令久屈。

translations.literal: During Yanchang, an edict said: "Yizong is an elder of the former reign and has served diligently on the frontier. We should not make the land wait for the man and so leave him long in frustration.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanchang, an edict said: "Yizong is an elder of the former reign and has served diligently on the frontier. We should not make the land wait for the man and so leave him long in frustration.

sentences.zh: 可使持節、鎮東將軍、濟州刺史，常侍如故。」

translations.literal: He may be made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the East, and Governor of Jizhou, with Palace Attendant as before."
translations.idiomatic: He may be made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Guards the East, and Governor of Jizhou, with Palace Attendant as before."

sentences.zh: 世宗慮其不受代，遣後將軍李世哲與桃符率眾襲之，出其不意，奄入廣陵。

translations.literal: Shizong feared he would not accept replacement and sent Rear General Li Shizhe with Taofu and troops to seize him by surprise, suddenly entering Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhe and Taofu seized Guangling by surprise.

sentences.zh: 益宗子魯生、魯賢等奔於關南，招引賊兵，襲逐諸戍，光城已南皆為賊所保。

translations.literal: Yizong's sons Lusheng and Luxian and the rest fled to the pass south, drew bandit troops, chased the garrisons, and south of Guangcheng all was held by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sons fled south and bandits held Guangcheng south.

sentences.zh: 世哲討擊破之，復置郡戍，而以益宗還。

translations.literal: Shizhe struck and broke them, reset garrisons, and Yizong was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhe beat them and Yizong was restored.

sentences.zh: 授征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，改封曲陽縣開國伯。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Conquers the South, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, added Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, fief changed to Baron of Quyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was given golden seal, scattered-cavalry attendant, and Baron of Quyang.

sentences.zh: 益宗生長邊地，不願內榮，雖位秩崇重，猶以為恨，上表曰：「臣昔在南，仰餐皇化，擁率部曲三千餘家，棄彼邊榮，歸投樂土，兄弟荼炭，釁結賊朝。

translations.literal: Yizong had grown up on the frontier and did not want inner honors; although his rank and salary were lofty, he still felt it as a grievance and submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly, when I was in the south, I looked up and partook of imperial transformation, led more than three thousand families of my followers, abandoned that frontier honor, and turned to the happy land. My brothers were plunged into suffering, and enmity was tied with the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had grown up on the frontier and did not want inner honors; although his rank and salary were lofty, he still felt it as a grievance and submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly, when I was in the south, I looked up and partook of imperial transformation, led more than three thousand families of my followers, abandoned that frontier honor, and turned to the happy land. My brothers were plunged into suffering, and enmity was tied with the rebel court.

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝錄臣乃誠，授以藩任。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen recorded my sincerity and entrusted me with a frontier office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen recorded my sincerity and entrusted me with a frontier office.

sentences.zh: 方欲仰憑國威，冀雪冤耻，豈容背寵向讎，就險危命。

translations.literal: I wished to rely on the state’s authority and hoped to wash away wrong and shame; how could I turn my back on favor, face an enemy, and seek a dangerous fate?
translations.idiomatic: I wished to rely on the state’s authority and hoped to wash away wrong and shame; how could I turn my back on favor, face an enemy, and seek a dangerous fate?

sentences.zh: 昔郢豫紛擾，臣躬率義兵，擁絕賊路，竊謂誠心，仰簡朝野。

translations.literal: In past years, when Ying and Yu were in turmoil, I personally led loyal troops, cut off the enemy route, and privately thought that my sincere heart was clear to court and countryside above.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, when Ying and Yu were in turmoil, I personally led loyal troops, cut off the enemy route, and privately thought that my sincere heart was clear to court and countryside above.

sentences.zh: 但任重據邊，易招塵謗，致使桃符橫加讒毀，說臣恒欲投南，暴亂非一。

translations.literal: But because my charge was heavy and I occupied the frontier, dust and slander were easily invited, causing Taofu to add slanders wantonly, saying that I constantly wanted to defect south and that my violence and disorder were not a single matter.
translations.idiomatic: But because my charge was heavy and I occupied the frontier, dust and slander were easily invited, causing Taofu to add slanders wantonly, saying that I constantly wanted to defect south and that my violence and disorder were not a single matter.

sentences.zh: 乞檢事原，以何為驗？

translations.literal: I beg that the matter be investigated to its source: what evidence is there?
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the matter be investigated to its source: what evidence is there?

sentences.zh: 復云虐害番兵，殺賣過半，如其所言，未審死失之家，所訟有幾？

translations.literal: He further says that I cruelly harmed the tribal soldiers, killing and selling more than half of them. If what he says is true, I do not know how many households of the dead and lost have filed complaints.
translations.idiomatic: He further says that I cruelly harmed the tribal soldiers, killing and selling more than half of them. If what he says is true, I do not know how many households of the dead and lost have filed complaints.

sentences.zh: 又云耗官粟帛，倉庫傾盡。

translations.literal: He also says that I consumed official grain and silk until the granaries and storehouses were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: He also says that I consumed official grain and silk until the granaries and storehouses were emptied.

sentences.zh: 御史覆檢，曾無損折。

translations.literal: When the censor rechecked them, there had been no loss at all.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor rechecked them, there had been no loss at all.

sentences.zh: 初代之日，二子魯生、魯賢、從子超秀等並在城中，安然無二，而桃符密遣積射將軍鹿永固私將甲士，打息魯生，僅得存命。

translations.literal: On the day I was first replaced, my two sons Lusheng and Luxian, my nephew Chaoxiu, and the others were all inside the city, peaceful and without second thoughts, but Taofu secretly sent General of Accumulated Archers Lu Yonggu with armored soldiers privately to attack my son Lusheng, who barely survived with his life.
translations.idiomatic: On the day I was first replaced, my two sons Lusheng and Luxian, my nephew Chaoxiu, and the others were all inside the city, peaceful and without second thoughts, but Taofu secretly sent General of Accumulated Archers Lu Yonggu with armored soldiers privately to attack my son Lusheng, who barely survived with his life.

sentences.zh: 唱云：『我被面敕，若能得魯生、魯賢首者，各賞本郡。』

translations.literal: They proclaimed: If we can get the heads of Lusheng and Luxian, each will be rewarded with his original commandery.
translations.idiomatic: They proclaimed: If we can get the heads of Lusheng and Luxian, each will be rewarded with his original commandery.

sentences.zh: 士馬圍遶，騰城唱殺，二息戰怖，實由於此。

translations.literal: Horsemen and soldiers surrounded them, rushed up the city wall, and shouted kill; the terror of my two sons truly arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Horsemen and soldiers surrounded them, rushed up the city wall, and shouted kill; the terror of my two sons truly arose from this.

sentences.zh: 殘敗居業，為生蕩然，乃復毀發墳墓，露泄枯骸。

translations.literal: Their residence and livelihood were ruined and swept away, and then graves were destroyed and dried bones exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Their residence and livelihood were ruined and swept away, and then graves were destroyed and dried bones exposed.

sentences.zh: 存者罹生離之苦，亡魂遭粉骨之痛。

translations.literal: The living suffered the pain of separation while alive, and the souls of the dead suffered the agony of shattered bones.
translations.idiomatic: The living suffered the pain of separation while alive, and the souls of the dead suffered the agony of shattered bones.

sentences.zh: 昔歲朝廷頻遣桃符數加慰勞，而桃符凶姦，擅生禍福，云『唯我相申，致降恩旨』。

translations.literal: In past years, the court repeatedly sent Taofu to comfort and reward me several times, but Taofu was fierce and treacherous and arbitrarily created disaster and blessing, saying: Only I can explain matters for you and bring down gracious commands.
translations.idiomatic: In past years, the court repeatedly sent Taofu to comfort and reward me several times, but Taofu was fierce and treacherous and arbitrarily created disaster and blessing, saying: Only I can explain matters for you and bring down gracious commands.

sentences.zh: 及返京師，復欺朝廷，說臣父子全無忠誠，誣陷貞良，惑亂朝聽。

translations.literal: When he returned to the capital, he again deceived the court, saying that my father and sons had no loyalty at all, falsely accusing the loyal and good and confusing the court’s hearing.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, he again deceived the court, saying that my father and sons had no loyalty at all, falsely accusing the loyal and good and confusing the court’s hearing.

sentences.zh: 乞攝桃符與臣並對，若臣罪有狀，分從憲網；

translations.literal: I beg that Taofu be summoned to confront me together. If my crimes have evidence, I will accept the net of the law according to my share;
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Taofu be summoned to confront me together. If my crimes have evidence, I will accept the net of the law according to my share;

sentences.zh: 如桃符是謬，坐宜有歸。」

translations.literal: if Taofu is wrong, the guilt should have somewhere to return."
translations.idiomatic: if Taofu is wrong, the guilt should have somewhere to return."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「既經大宥，不容方更為獄。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Since there has already been a great pardon, it is not permissible now to make another case."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Since there has already been a great pardon, it is not permissible now to make another case."

sentences.zh: 熙平初，益宗又表乞東豫，以招二子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, Yizong again memorialized begging Eastern Yu to win back his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping he begged Eastern Yu to recover his sons.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令曰：「卿誠著二朝，勳光南服，作藩萬里，列土承家，前朝往恩，酬敍不淺。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling issued an order saying: "Your sincerity was manifest in two reigns, and your merit shone over the southern lands. You served as a frontier screen ten thousand li away, held territory, and carried on your house; the former reign’s grace in rewarding and ranking you was not shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling issued an order saying: "Your sincerity was manifest in two reigns, and your merit shone over the southern lands. You served as a frontier screen ten thousand li away, held territory, and carried on your house; the former reign’s grace in rewarding and ranking you was not shallow.

sentences.zh: 兼子弟荷榮，中表被澤，相□輕重，卿所知悉。

translations.literal: Moreover, your sons and younger kin received honors, and your inner and outer relatives were covered with favor; when weighed against one another, you know all this well.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your sons and younger kin received honors, and your inner and outer relatives were covered with favor; when weighed against one another, you know all this well.

sentences.zh: 先帝以卿勞舊，州小祿薄，故遷牧華壤，爰登顯級。

translations.literal: The late emperor, because you were old in service and merit and because the province was small and its salary thin, moved you to govern a rich land and raised you to a conspicuous rank.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, because you were old in service and merit and because the province was small and its salary thin, moved you to govern a rich land and raised you to a conspicuous rank.

sentences.zh: 于時番兵交換，不生猜疑，而卿息魯賢等無事外叛，忠孝俱乖，翻為戎首。

translations.literal: At that time, when tribal troops were exchanged, no suspicion was born, yet your sons Luxian and the others, without cause, rebelled abroad, violating both loyalty and filiality and turning into leaders of the Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, when tribal troops were exchanged, no suspicion was born, yet your sons Luxian and the others, without cause, rebelled abroad, violating both loyalty and filiality and turning into leaders of the Rong.

sentences.zh: 以卿誠重，不復相計。

translations.literal: Because your sincerity is weighty, this was not further counted against you.
translations.idiomatic: Because your sincerity is weighty, this was not further counted against you.

sentences.zh: 今臥護征南，榮以金紫，朝廷處遇，又甚於先。

translations.literal: Now you hold office in reserve as General Who Campaigns South and are honored with Gold and Purple; the court’s treatment of you is even greater than before.
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold office in reserve as General Who Campaigns South and are honored with Gold and Purple; the court’s treatment of you is even greater than before.

sentences.zh: 且卿年老，方就閑養，焉得以本州為念？

translations.literal: Besides, you are old and should now take leisure and nourishment; how can you keep thinking of your original province?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you are old and should now take leisure and nourishment; how can you keep thinking of your original province?

sentences.zh: 魯賢來否，豈待自往也，但遣慰納，足相昭亮。

translations.literal: Whether Luxian comes or not, how could it require you to go yourself? It is enough simply to send comfort and acceptance to make matters clear.
translations.idiomatic: Whether Luxian comes or not, how could it require you to go yourself? It is enough simply to send comfort and acceptance to make matters clear.

sentences.zh: 若審遣信，當更啟聞，別敕東豫，聽卿喻曉魯賢。」

translations.literal: If you truly send a messenger, you should report again, and I will separately command Eastern Yu to allow you to instruct and enlighten Luxian."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly send a messenger, you should report again, and I will separately command Eastern Yu to allow you to instruct and enlighten Luxian."

sentences.zh: 二年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year two at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 贈征東大將軍、郢州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumously General Who Conquers the East and Ying governor, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously eastern conqueror and Ying governor, posthumous Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 少子纂，襲封。

translations.literal: The youngest son Zuan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Youngest son Zuan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 位至征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He rose to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Scattered Cavalry Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He became barbarian-conqueror and scattered-cavalry grandee.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左將軍、東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Left General and Eastern Yu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Left General and Eastern Yu governor.

sentences.zh: 益宗長子隨興，冠軍將軍、平原太守。

translations.literal: Yizong's eldest son Suixing was General Who Champions the Army and Pingyuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Suixing was champion general and Pingyuan governor.

sentences.zh: 隨興情貪邊官，不願內地，改授弋陽、汝南二郡太守。

translations.literal: Suixing was greedy for border office and unwilling for the interior; he was changed to Yiyang and Runan governors.
translations.idiomatic: Suixing preferred the border and took Yiyang and Runan.

sentences.zh: 益宗兄興祖，太和末，亦來歸附。

translations.literal: Yizong's elder brother Xingzu at the end of Taihe also came to attach.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Xingzu surrendered late in Taihe.

sentences.zh: 景明中，假郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In Jingming he was Acting Ying governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming he was acting Ying governor.

sentences.zh: 及義陽置郢州，改授征虜將軍、江州刺史，詔賜朝服、劍舄一具，治麻城。

translations.literal: When Yiyang was made Ying Province, he was made General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Jiang governor; an edict granted court dress, sword and shoes one set, administering Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province made him Jiang governor at Macheng with court dress.

sentences.zh: 興祖卒，益宗請隨興代之，世宗不許，罷并東豫。

translations.literal: Xingzu died; Yizong begged Suixing to replace him; Shizong did not permit and abolished and merged Eastern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingzu died, Eastern Yu was abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，益州內附之後，蕭鸞遣寧州刺史董巒追討之，官軍進擊，執巒并其子景曜，送於行宮。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Yi Province submitted, Xiao Luan sent Ning governor Dong Luan to pursue; the government army attacked and seized Luan and his son Jingyao, sending them to the mobile palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi submitted, Dong Luan was captured with son Jingyao.

sentences.zh: 巒，字仲舒，營陽人。

translations.literal: Luan, courtesy name Zhongshu, was a man of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luan of Yingyang, styled Zhongshu.

sentences.zh: 真君末，隨父南叛。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenjun he followed his father in southern rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenjun he fled south with his father.

sentences.zh: 雖長自江外，言語風氣猶同華夏。

translations.literal: Though he grew up beyond the river, speech and manners were still like Huaxia.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the south, he still seemed Chinese.

sentences.zh: 性疏武，不多識文字。

translations.literal: By nature he was coarse in martial matters and did not know many written characters.
translations.idiomatic: He was martial and barely literate.

sentences.zh: 高祖引巒於庭，問其南事，巒怖不能對，數顧景曜。

translations.literal: Gaozu received Luan in the courtyard and asked southern affairs; Luan was afraid and could not answer, repeatedly looking at Jingyao.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu questioned him; he could only look to Jingyao.

sentences.zh: 景曜進代父答，申敍蕭鸞篡襲始終，辭理橫出，言非而辯，高祖異焉。

translations.literal: Jingyao stepped forward to answer for his father, narrating Xiao Luan's usurpation from start to finish; the reasoning burst forth, the words wrong yet eloquent—Gaozu marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyao answered brilliantly about Luan's usurpation; Gaozu marveled.

sentences.zh: 以巒為越騎校尉，景曜為員外郎。

translations.literal: Luan was made Valiant Cavalry Commandant, Jingyao outer aide.
translations.idiomatic: Luan was Valiant Cavalry Commandant; Jingyao outer aide.

sentences.zh: 謀欲南叛，坐徙朔州。

translations.literal: Plotting southern rebellion, he was punished by exile to Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Plotting south, he was exiled to Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南討漢陽，召巒從軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south against Hanyang, Luan was summoned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for the Hanyang campaign.

sentences.zh: 景曜至洛陽，密啟其父必當奔叛。

translations.literal: Jingyao reached Luoyang and secretly reported his father would surely flee in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyao warned his father would rebel.

sentences.zh: 軍次魯陽，巒單騎南走，過南陽、新野，歷告二城以魏軍當至，戒之備防。

translations.literal: The army reached Luyang; Luan alone on horseback fled south, passing Nanyang and Xinye, everywhere telling the two cities the Wei army was coming and warning them to prepare defense.
translations.idiomatic: At Luyang Luan fled south warning cities.

sentences.zh: 房伯玉、劉忌並云無足可慮。

translations.literal: Fang Boyu and Liu Ji both said there was nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Boyu and Liu Ji dismissed the threat.

sentences.zh: 巒曰：「不然，軍勢甚盛。」

translations.literal: Luan said: "It is not so; the army’s power is very great."
translations.idiomatic: Luan said: "It is not so; the army’s power is very great."

sentences.zh: 至境首北向哭呼景曜云：「吾百口在彼，事理須還，不得顧汝一子也。」

translations.literal: When he reached the border, he faced north, wept, and called out to Jingyao, saying: "My hundred mouths are there; by the logic of the matter I must return, and cannot look after you, one son."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the border, he faced north, wept, and called out to Jingyao, saying: "My hundred mouths are there; by the logic of the matter I must return, and cannot look after you, one son."

sentences.zh: 景曜鎖詣行在所，數而斬之。

translations.literal: Jingyao was chained to the place of the imperial progress and several times beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyao was chained and executed.

sentences.zh: 又有陳伯之者，下邳人也。

translations.literal: There was also Chen Bozhi, a man of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 以勇力自効，仕於江南，為鎮南大將軍、江州刺史、豐城縣開國公。

translations.literal: He offered his valor and strength, served in the south, and was General Who Pacifies the South, Jiang governor, and Baron of Fengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He served the south as southern conqueror, Jiang governor, and Fengcheng baron.

sentences.zh: 景明三年，伯之遣使密表請降，并遣其子冠軍將軍、徐州刺史、永昌縣開國侯虎牙為質。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming, Bozhi sent envoys with a secret memorial requesting surrender and sent his son the champion general, Xu governor, and Baron of Yongchang Huya as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year three he secretly offered surrender and sent son Huya as hostage.

sentences.zh: 四年，以伯之為持節、都督江郢二州諸軍事、平南將軍、江州刺史、曲江縣開國公，邑一千戶；

translations.literal: In the fourth year Bozhi was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander over Jiang and Ying military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, Jiang governor, and Duke of Qujiang county with one thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: Year four he was made Jiang duke with staff and command;

sentences.zh: 虎牙為冠軍將軍、員外散騎常侍、豫寧縣開國伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Huya was General Who Champions the Army, outer Scattered-Cavalry Attendant, and Baron of Yuning with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Huya was champion general and Yuning baron.

sentences.zh: 正始初，蕭衍征虜將軍趙祖悅築城於水東，與潁川接對，置兵數千，欲為攻討之本。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi, Xiao Yan's General Who Conquers the Barbarians Zhao Zuyue built a city east of the water facing Yingchuan, placing several thousand troops as a base for attack.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengshi Zhao Zuyue built east of Yingchuan with thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 伯之進軍討祖悅，大破之，乘勝長驅入城，刺祖悅三創，賊眾大敗。

translations.literal: Bozhi advanced to attack Zuyue and routed him, riding victory in long drive into the city, stabbing Zuyue three wounds—the bandit host was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi routed Zuyue, entered the city, and wounded him thrice.

sentences.zh: 進討南城，破賊諸部，斬獲數千。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Nancheng he broke the bandit divisions, beheading and capturing several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He took Nancheng and thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，除伯之光祿大夫，虎牙遷前軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second summer he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Huya was promoted Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: Second summer he became Grand Master; Huya Forward General.

translations.literal: Collation mark ten—the received text here is incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note 10: lacuna in the received text.]

sentences.zh: 孟表，字武達，濟北蛇丘人也。

translations.literal: Meng Biao, courtesy name Wuda, was a man of Sheqiu in Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Biao of Sheqiu in Jibei, styled Wuda.

sentences.zh: 自云本屬北地，號索里諸孟。

translations.literal: He said his origin was originally Beidi, called the Suoli clan of Meng.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed Beidi origin, Suoli Meng clan.

sentences.zh: 青徐內屬後，表因事南渡，仕蕭鸞為馬頭太守。

translations.literal: After Qing and Xu submitted within, Biao because of events crossed south and served Xiao Luan as Matou governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Qing-Xu submission he went south as Matou governor under Luan.

sentences.zh: 太和十八年，表據郡歸誠，除輔國將軍、南兗州刺史，領馬頭太守，賜爵譙縣侯，鎮渦陽。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Taihe, Biao held the commandery in allegiance and was made General Who Assists the State, southern Yan governor, holding Matou governorship, enfeoffed Marquis of Qiao, garrisoning Guoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year eighteen he surrendered and garrisoned Guoyang as Qiao marquis.

sentences.zh: 後蕭鸞遣其豫州刺史裴叔業攻圍六十餘日，城中食盡，唯以朽革及草木皮葉為粮。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Luan sent his Yu governor Pei Shuye to besiege more than sixty days; food in the city was exhausted and only rotten hides and tree bark and leaves were grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye besieged sixty days until they ate bark and hides.

sentences.zh: 表撫循將士，勠力固守。

translations.literal: Biao comforted and led the officers and soldiers, striving together to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Biao rallied the garrison to hold.

sentences.zh: 會鎮南將軍王肅解義陽之圍，還以救之，叔業乃退。

translations.literal: When Pacify-the-South Wang Su lifted the siege of Yiyang and returned to rescue, Shuye then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su relieved Yiyang and Shuye withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，有一南人，自云姓邊字叔珍，攜妻息從壽春投表，云慕化歸國。

translations.literal: Earlier a southerner surnamed Bian styled Shuzhen brought wife and children from Shouchun to Biao, saying he admired transformation and returned to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A southerner Bian Shuzhen came claiming to defect.

sentences.zh: 未及送闕，便值叔業圍城。

translations.literal: Before he could be sent to court, Shuye besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached court the siege began.

sentences.zh: 表後察叔珍言色，頗疑有異，即加推覈，乃云是叔業姑兒，為叔業所遣，規為內應，所攜妻子並亦假妄。

translations.literal: Biao later observed Shuzhen's words and color and greatly suspected something odd; on pushing investigation it was that he was Shuye's nephew by a sister, sent by Shuye, plotting as inside agent—the wife and children carried were also false.
translations.idiomatic: Biao found him Shuye's spy; family was fake.

sentences.zh: 表出叔珍於北門外斬之，於是人情乃安。

translations.literal: Biao executed Shuzhen outside the north gate, and then popular feeling was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Shuzhen at the north gate and calm returned.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其誠績，封汶陽縣開國伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised his loyal achievement and enfeoffed him Baron of Wenyang county with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made him Baron of Wenyang at five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、濟州刺史，為散騎常侍、光祿大夫，進號平西將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Ji governor, made Scattered-Cavalry Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, title advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He became barbarian-conqueror, Ji governor, grand master, and western conqueror.

sentences.zh: 世宗末，降平東將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Shizong he was reduced to General Who Pacifies the East and Qi governor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shizong he was eastern conqueror and Qi governor.

sentences.zh: 延昌四年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yan chang he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yan chang year four at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、兗州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously General Who Pacifies the East and Yan governor, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously eastern conqueror and Yan governor, posthumous Gong.

sentences.zh: 子崇，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Chong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 官至昌黎、濟北二郡太守。

translations.literal: He rose to governor of Changli and Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Changli and Jibei.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：薛安都一武夫耳，雖輕於去就，實啟東南。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xue Andou was only a martial man; though light in going and coming, he truly opened the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says Andou, though fickle, opened the southeast.

sentences.zh: 事窘圖變，而竟保寵秩，優矣。

translations.literal: Pressed by events he plotted change, yet in the end kept favor and rank—well done.
translations.idiomatic: He kept favor despite his plots.

sentences.zh: 真度一謀，見賞明主。

translations.literal: Zhendu's one plan was appreciated by a bright lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu's counsel won a bright lord's praise.

sentences.zh: 眾敬舉地納誠，榮曜朝國，人位並列，無乏於時。

translations.literal: Zhongjing offered land and allegiance, glory shining in the court state; men and posts all ranked together without lack in the time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing's surrender brought glory; Bi and allies shared rank.

sentences.zh: 文秀不回，有死節之氣，非但身蒙嘉禮，乃至子免刑戮。

translations.literal: Wenxiu did not turn back and had the spirit of dying for integrity; not only he himself received gracious rites, but even his son was spared capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu's integrity won grace for his son.

sentences.zh: 在我欲其罵人，忠義可不勉也。

translations.literal: In our state we desire men to curse the enemy—how can loyalty not be encouraged!
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty to one's state deserves encouragement.

sentences.zh: 張讜觀機委質，篤恤流離，亦仁智矣。
