translations.literal: Zhang Dang saw the moment and offered his person, earnest in soothing the displaced—also benevolent and wise.
translations.idiomatic: Dang was humane and wise in his surrender and care.

sentences.zh: 田益宗蠻夷荒帥，翻然效款，終懷金曳紫，不其美歟！

translations.literal: Tian Yizong, a barbarian chieftain of the wild, suddenly turned in allegiance, and to the end trailed gold and dragged purple—is it not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Yizong the Man chief ended in purple and gold.

sentences.zh: 孟表之致名位，非徒然也。

translations.literal: Meng Biao's attaining name and rank was not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Biao earned his fame.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 與東雍州刺史沮渠秉謀逆 諸本「秉」作「康」。

translations.literal: Plotting rebellion with Eastern Yong Governor Juqu Bing: all editions read "Kang" for "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: On Juqu Bing vs. "Kang" in editions:

sentences.zh: 按卷四下世祖紀下太平真君五年七月和卷九九沮渠蒙遜傳都作「沮渠秉」。

translations.literal: According to juan 4B, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu, seventh month of Taiping Zhenjun 5, and juan 99, Biography of Juqu Mengxun, both write "Juqu Bing."
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 4B, Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu, seventh month of Taiping Zhenjun 5, and juan 99, Biography of Juqu Mengxun, both write "Juqu Bing."

sentences.zh: 北史卷三九薛安都傳作「康」，卷九三北涼沮渠氏傳作「季義」。

translations.literal: Beishi, juan 39, Biography of Xue Andou, writes "Kang," while juan 93, Biography of the Juqu clan of Northern Liang, writes "Jiyi."
translations.idiomatic: Beishi, juan 39, Biography of Xue Andou, writes "Kang," while juan 93, Biography of the Juqu clan of Northern Liang, writes "Jiyi."

sentences.zh: 其人本名「秉」，字「季義」，北史避唐諱，改「秉」為「康」，或稱其字。

translations.literal: His original name was "Bing" and his style was "Jiyi"; Beishi avoided the Tang taboo and changed "Bing" to "Kang," or else referred to him by his style.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was "Bing" and his style was "Jiyi"; Beishi avoided the Tang taboo and changed "Bing" to "Kang," or else referred to him by his style.

sentences.zh: 魏書本皆作「秉」，這裏當是後人據北史改，今回改。

translations.literal: The Wei shu text originally always wrote "Bing"; here later people must have changed it according to Beishi, so it is now changed back.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu text originally always wrote "Bing"; here later people must have changed it according to Beishi, so it is now changed back.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍秦州刺史河東王 按此傳載安都及其子孫生前曾任、或死後追贈秦州刺史的共五人。

translations.literal: Posthumously made general of original rank, Qin governor, Prince of Hedong: this biography records five who held or were posthumously made Qin governor.
translations.idiomatic: Five in this chapter held Qin governor—likely Taizhou error:

sentences.zh: 疑皆「泰州」之訛。

translations.literal: They are probably all corruptions of "Taizhou."
translations.idiomatic: They are probably all corruptions of "Taizhou."

sentences.zh: 泰州治河東蒲坂，是薛氏本州，當時以官本州刺史為榮，故祖孫多居此官。

translations.literal: Taizhou seat was Hedong Puban, the Xue clan's home province; at the time holding home-province governor was honor.
translations.idiomatic: Puban in Hedong was the Xue homeland.

sentences.zh: 若是秦州，和薛氏毫無關係，便不可解。

translations.literal: If Qinzhou, it has no relation to the Xue and is inexplicable.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou does not fit the Xue.

sentences.zh: 又此州雖或先曾有「秦州」之稱，但此時早已名「泰州」，參卷一０六下地形志下校記泰州條。

translations.literal: Moreover, although this province may once earlier have been called "Qinzhou," by this time it had long been named "Taizhou"; see the collation note on Taizhou in juan 106B, Treatise on Terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, although this province may once earlier have been called "Qinzhou," by this time it had long been named "Taizhou"; see the collation note on Taizhou in juan 106B, Treatise on Terrain.

sentences.zh: 拜奉車都尉 諸本「車」下有「騎」字。

translations.literal: Made Bearer of the Imperial Carriage: all editions have an extra "Cavalry" under "Carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Extra "Cavalry" in Bearer of Imperial Carriage is spurious:

sentences.zh: 按「奉車都尉」見卷一一三官氏志太和前、後職令，「騎」字衍，今刪。

translations.literal: The office tables before and after Taihe in juan 113, Treatise on Offices and Clans, have "Commandant of Imperial Carriages"; the character "qi" is redundant and is now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The office tables before and after Taihe in juan 113, Treatise on Offices and Clans, have "Commandant of Imperial Carriages"; the character "qi" is redundant and is now deleted.

sentences.zh: 會安都引國授軍經其城下 按「授」當是「援」之訛。

translations.literal: When Andou led the state’s aid army past the city walls: "shou" should be a corruption of "yuan."
translations.idiomatic: In the phrase about Andou leading the relief army past the walls, "shou" should read "yuan," aid.

sentences.zh: 天平中 諸本「天」作「太」。

translations.literal: During Tianping. All editions write "tian" as "tai."
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping. All editions write "tian" as "tai."

sentences.zh: 按「太平」無此年號。

translations.literal: There is no reign title "Taiping" here.
translations.idiomatic: There is no reign title "Taiping" here.

sentences.zh: 下云：「與舍人韋鴻坐泄密，賜盡於宅。」

translations.literal: Below it says: "Together with Palace Attendant Wei Hong, he was implicated in leaking secrets and was ordered to die at home."
translations.idiomatic: Below it says: "Together with Palace Attendant Wei Hong, he was implicated in leaking secrets and was ordered to die at home."

sentences.zh: 韋鴻附見卷四五韋閬傳，事在「天平三年」。

translations.literal: Wei Hong is attached to the biography of Wei Lang in juan 45; the matter occurred in "Tianping year three."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hong is attached to the biography of Wei Lang in juan 45; the matter occurred in "Tianping year three."

sentences.zh: 「太」乃「天」形近而訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Tai" is a graphically similar corruption of "tian" and is now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: "Tai" is a graphically similar corruption of "tian" and is now corrected.

sentences.zh: 元茂 按「元茂」不知何人。

translations.literal: Yuan Mao. It is unknown who "Yuan Mao" was.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mao. It is unknown who "Yuan Mao" was.

sentences.zh: 上文稱「讜兄弟十人」，但只舉「兄忠」一人，「元茂」當是讜兄弟之後，上有脫文。

translations.literal: Above, the text says "Dang’s ten brothers," but it mentions only one person, elder brother Zhong; "Yuan Mao" should come after Dang’s brothers, and there is missing text above.
translations.idiomatic: Above, the text says "Dang’s ten brothers," but it mentions only one person, elder brother Zhong; "Yuan Mao" should come after Dang’s brothers, and there is missing text above.

sentences.zh: 景明初蕭衍遣軍主吳子陽率眾寇三關 按卷八世宗紀景明元年

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming Xiao Yan sent Wu Ziyang: according to annals Jingming year one
translations.idiomatic: Jingming year one annals:

sentences.zh: 九月乙丑記：「東豫州刺史田益宗破蕭寶卷將吳子陽、鄧元起於長風。」

translations.literal: The yichou day in the ninth month records: "Tian Yizong, Governor of Eastern Yuzhou, defeated Xiao Baojuan’s generals Wu Ziyang and Deng Yuanqi at Changfeng."
translations.idiomatic: The yichou day in the ninth month records: "Tian Yizong, Governor of Eastern Yuzhou, defeated Xiao Baojuan’s generals Wu Ziyang and Deng Yuanqi at Changfeng."

sentences.zh: 這年十一月蕭衍才起兵反寶卷。

translations.literal: That year eleventh month Xiao Yan only then rose against Baojuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan rebelled eleventh month that year.

sentences.zh: 吳子陽乃蕭寶卷將，稱蕭衍軍主誤。

translations.literal: Wu Ziyang was Baojuan's general—calling him Xiao Yan's army commander is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ziyang served Baojuan, not Yan.

sentences.zh: 下文「蕭衍建寧太守黃天賜築城赤亭」，據世宗紀，事在景明二年七月，亦稱「蕭寶卷將黃天賜」。

translations.literal: Below, the phrase "Xiao Yan’s Jianning administrator Huang Tianci built a fort at Chiting" refers, according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong, to the seventh month of Jingming 2, where Huang Tianci is also called "Xiao Baojuan’s general Huang Tianci."
translations.idiomatic: Below, the phrase "Xiao Yan’s Jianning administrator Huang Tianci built a fort at Chiting" refers, according to the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizong, to the seventh month of Jingming 2, where Huang Tianci is also called "Xiao Baojuan’s general Huang Tianci."

sentences.zh: 此傳兩「蕭衍」均當作「寶卷」。

translations.literal: Both instances of "Xiao Yan" in this biography should be "Baojuan."
translations.idiomatic: Both instances of "Xiao Yan" in this biography should be "Baojuan."

sentences.zh: 竊惟蕭衍亂常 諸本「亂」字空格或注「闕」字，今據通鑑卷一四一

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Xiao Yan disrupted the norms: the editions leave a blank or note a lacuna for "luan"; it is now supplied from Zizhi tongjian, juan 141.
translations.idiomatic: In “Xiao Yan disrupted the norms,” the editions leave a blank or mark a lacuna for "luan"; the character is supplied from Zizhi tongjian 141.

sentences.zh: 〈四五０四頁〉

translations.literal: 〈4504 pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈4504 pages〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: supplemented.

sentences.zh: 無暇外維州鎮 諸本「無」字上注「闕」字，「無」字下無「暇」字，今據通鑑

translations.literal: No leisure to maintain the outer provinces and garrisons: the editions note a lacuna above "wu" and lack "xia" below it; this is now corrected from the Tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: For “no leisure to maintain the outer provinces and garrisons,” the editions mark a lacuna before "wu" and omit "xia" after it; corrected from the Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same volume pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same volume pages〉

sentences.zh: 補。

translations.literal: supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: supplemented.

sentences.zh: 二年夏除伯之光祿大夫虎牙遷前軍將軍 按伯之於次年二月敗梁將昌義之於梁城，隨即奔梁，見卷八世宗紀，其子虎牙為魏所殺，見梁書卷二０陳伯之傳。

translations.literal: Second year summer made Bozhi Grand Master: Bozhi next year second month lost to Liang general Chang Yanzhi at Liangcheng then fled Liang—annals and Chen Bozhi biography; son Huya killed by Wei—text incomplete, lacuna likely.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi narrative incomplete—likely lacuna before Liang flight.

sentences.zh: 此傳敍事不完，當有脫文。

translations.literal: This biography’s narrative is incomplete; there must be missing text.
translations.idiomatic: The narrative in this biography is incomplete; there must be a lacuna.

sentences.zh: 世宗末降平東將軍 按上文稱「進號平西將軍」，由「平西」改「平東」，不能說是「降」號。

translations.literal: At the end of Shizong’s reign, demoted to General Who Pacifies the East. Above, the text says "advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West"; changing from "Pacifies the West" to "Pacifies the East" cannot be called a demotion.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shizong’s reign, demoted to General Who Pacifies the East. Above, the text says "advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the West"; changing from "Pacifies the West" to "Pacifies the East" cannot be called a demotion.

sentences.zh: 疑「降」 字訛或衍。

translations.literal: It is suspected that "jiang" is either corrupt or redundant.
translations.idiomatic: The word "jiang" is probably corrupt or intrusive.

sentences.zh: 否則「世宗末」上脫去孟表由「平西」進升軍號事。

translations.literal: Otherwise, above "at the end of Shizong’s reign" there is missing text about Meng Biao being promoted in military title from "Pacifies the West."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, above "at the end of Shizong’s reign" there is missing text about Meng Biao being promoted in military title from "Pacifies the West."
